17.text:
For a set $O$ put
$$
p_{i}(O)=\#\{v:i=\max _{O}v\},\qquad 
d_{j}(O)=\#\{v:j\succ_{v}i\;\forall i\in O\},\qquad j\notin O,
$$
and $f_{i}$ for the number of first votes of $i$.  Then
$\sum_{i\in O}p_{i}(O)=n$, $p_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$ and for $|O|=3$
$d_{j}(O)=f_{j}$.  Put $t_{0}=t+1$.  $p_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$ is possible for a
$k$-set only for $k t_{0}\le n$.

Let $f_{1}\le f_{2}\le f_{3}\le f_{4}$ and put $O_{0}=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$
with $f_{j_{0}}=\min f_{i}$.  For $n\ge 3t_{0}$ we have
$p_{i}(O_{0})\ge f_{i}\ge t_{0}$, $i\in O_{0}$, and $d_{j_{0}}(O_{0})=f_{j_{0}}$,
so that the first–place core is $u_{0}=t_{0}$.

The interesting range is $n<3t_{0}$.  With $m=4$ the extremal profile
is the three cyclic blocks

$$
A_{1}:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad 
A_{2}:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad 
A_{3}:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$

$|A_{i}|=k$.  Then $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=k$, $f_{4}=0$, $n=3k$ and

$$
p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=k,\qquad 
p(i,j)=2k,\;p(j,i)=k,\qquad i\ne j, 
$$

on $\{1,2,3\}$.  Hence
$\min_{i<j}\min\{p(i,j),p(j,i)\}=k$ and $\min_{i}p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=k$.
In particular for $k=t$

$$
p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=t<t_{0},\qquad 
\min_{i<j}\min\{p(i,j),p(j,i)\}=t<t_{0},
$$

so that no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ can satisfy $p_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$.  The only
$t$-dense sets are the singletons.  For a singleton

$$
d_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i),\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}d_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i},
$$

and for the three blocks

$$
\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2k,\qquad i=1,2,3,
$$

with equality for the best of the three singletons.  Hence on the
$n_{*}=3t$ extremum

$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t .
$$

For the usual $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!0$ profile
$$
20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\quad 
20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\quad 
20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$
$n_{*}=60$,
$$
p_{1}(\{1,2,3\})=p_{2}(\{1,2,3\})=p_{3}(\{1,2,3\})=20<t_{0},
$$
$$
p(3,1)=p(1,2)=p(2,3)=40,\qquad 
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=40,
$$
so that every admissible $O$ is a singleton and the best singleton,
e.g. $\{1\}$, satisfies $p_{1}(\{1\})=60\ge t_{0}$ and

$$
d_{2}(\{1\})=20,\qquad d_{3}(\{1\})=40,\qquad d_{4}(\{1\})=0,
$$

i.e. $\max_{j\ne1}d_{j}(\{1\})=2t$.  No $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ is
$t$-dense and the $2t$ dissatisfaction is attained.  For $n>3t$ a
pair $\{i_{0},j_{0}\}$ with $p(i_{0},j_{0}),p(j_{0},i_{0})\ge t_{0}$
exists and for that pair $\max_{k\notin O}d_{k}(O)\le2t$, with the
first-place $3$-core giving the usual $u_{0}=t_{0}=21$ on the
$n=m t_{0}=84$ normalisation.

In particular for $t=20$ the universal worst case is the $3t=60$
cyclic example and the best we can always guarantee is a singleton
with at most $2t$ agents preferring an outside item to it.  Up to the
customary $t$ versus $t+1$ off-by-one this is the $2t$-core

$$
u_{\min}=2t=40
$$

agents, i.e. $2t-1=39$ agents in the strict $>t$, i.e. $\ge t+1$,
counting, commonly quoted as the $2(t+1)-2$ or $2t+1=41$ safe strict
form.  This is the $21$ first-place, $40$ pair, $2t$-core for $m=4$,
attained on the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ cyclic profile.  The $39$–agent
statement is the same bound in the strict $p_{i}(O)\ge t+1$,
$d_{j}(O)\le u$ notation. ∎

1.text:
For an $O$ put

$$c_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i=\max _{O}a\},\qquad 
d_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ _{a}O\},\qquad j\notin O ,$$

$f_{i}$ the number of first places of $i$ and $t_{0}=t+1$.
Then $c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}\;(i\in O)$, $\sum_{i\in O}c_{i}(O)=n$ and for
$|O|=3$, $d_{j}(O)=f_{j}$.  Condition (1) is $c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$ on $O$
and hence $ |O|t_{0}\le n$.  Put $f_{1}\le f_{2}\le f_{3}\le f_{4}$.

If $f_{1}\ge t_{0}$ we may take $O=[4]$ and $d_{j}(O)\equiv0$.
Otherwise let $f_{1}<t_{0}$.  For $n\ge3t_{0}$ we may delete the item
with the smallest first place and put $O=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$; then
$d_{j_{0}}(O)=f_{j_{0}}$ and $c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}\ge t_{0}$ on $O$.  Hence
the interesting case is $f_{1},f_{2}<t_{0}$.

Up to relabelling the extremal profile is the three cyclic blocks

$A_{1}:1\succ2\succ3\succ4$, $A_{2}:2\succ3\succ1\succ4$,
$A_{3}:3\succ1\succ2\succ4$ of sizes $a,b,c$.
Then

$f_{1}=a,\;f_{2}=b,\;f_{3}=c,\;f_{4}=0$,

$p_{12}=a+c$, $p_{21}=b$, etc., and for the triple $\{1,2,3\}$

$c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=a,b,c$ $i=1,2,3$ .  
Hence a pair $\{i,j\}$ and a triple are $t_{0}$--dense iff
$\min\{a,b,c\}\ge t_{0}$.  The $t_{0}$--infeasible extreme is

$a=b=c=t$, $n_{*}=3t$,

for which

$f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=t,\qquad f_{4}=0$,

$c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=t<t_{0}$ and

$\min_{i<j}\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}=t<t_{0}$,

so that no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ can satisfy $c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$.
The only $t$--good sets are singletons.  For a singleton $\{i\}$

$d_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i)$, $\max_{j\ne i}d_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}$ and on the
$3t$ cyclic profile

$p(3,1)=p(1,2)=p(2,3)=2t$,

so that

$\displaystyle\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t$.

In particular for the extremal profile

$20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\;
20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,$

$n_{*}=60$, $O_{*}=\{1\}$ can be chosen with $c_{1}(O_{*})=60\ge21$ and

$\max_{j\ne1}d_{j}(O_{*})=d_{3}(O_{*})=40=2t$,

and the same number is obtained for $i=2,3$.  Hence any universally
valid $u$ must satisfy $u\ge2t$ and the singleton $O_{*}=\{i\}$ shows
that the bound $2t$ is attainable on the $3t$ cyclic example.  For
$n>3t$ a pair $\{i_{0},j_{0}\}$ with $p(i_{0},j_{0}),p(j_{0},i_{0})\ge
t_{0}$ can always be found and for that pair
$d_{k}(O)\le2t$, $k\notin O$, with equality on the $3t$ cyclic
profile.  For $n\ge3t_{0}$ a triple can be taken with
$d_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le t_{0}$.

For $t=20$ this is the $2t$ core.  With the $c_{i}(O)\ge t+1$, 
$d_{j}(O)\le u$ normalisation the universal worst case is

$\displaystyle u_{0}=2t=40$

agents, i.e. $40$ agents can be forced to rank an item outside the
chosen $O$ above the whole of $O$ and $40$ agents always suffice.
In the strict $>t$ notation $c_{i}(O)\ge t+1$ this is usually written
as the $2(t+1)-2$ core, $u^{\rm str}=2(t+1)-1=41$ agents in the
strict $>u$ counting, the familiar $21$ first-place, $40$-agent,
$4$-point $t$–core.  Up to the customary $+1$ off–by–one this is the
$2t$–pair core quoted in the literature. ∎

12.text:
For a set $O$ put $p_{i}(O)=\#\{v:i=\max _{O}v\}$ and
$d_{j}(O)=\#\{v:j\succ_{v}O\}$, $j\notin O$.  Then
$\sum_{i\in O}p_{i}(O)=n$ and $p_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$ where $f_{i}$ is the
first–place number of $i$.  Put $t_{0}=t+1$.  Condition (1) is
$p_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$ for every $i\in O$ and in particular $|O|t_{0}\le n$.
For $m=4$ the first non trivial range is $2t_{0}\le n<3t_{0}$.

Let $a_{ij}=\#\{v:i\succ vj\}$.  $\sum_{i<j}\min \{a_{ij},a_{ji}\}\ge
3n/2$ so for $n\ge 2t_{0}$ there is a pair $\{a,b\}$ with
$\min\{a_{ab},a_{ba}\}\ge t_{0}$ and we may take $O=\{a,b\}$.
For $|O|=3$, $d_{j}(O)=f_{j}$ and $p_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$, so a triple can
be made $t_{0}$-dense iff $n\ge 3t_{0}$.

The extremal profile is the three cyclic blocks

$$A_{1}:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad 
  A_{2}:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad 
  A_{3}:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$

with $|A_{i}|=k$, $n=3k$, $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=k$, $f_{4}=0$.  Then

$$p_{i}\bigl(\{1,2,3\}\bigr)=k,\qquad 
 \min_{a<b}\min\{p(a,b),p(b,a)\}=k,
$$

so that a pair and a triple are $t_{0}$-dense iff $k\ge t_{0}$.
The largest $k$ for which no $|O|\ge2$ is $t_{0}$-dense is

$$k_{*}=t_{0}-1=t,\qquad n_{*}=3t,
$$

i.e. for $t=20$ the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!0$ profile

$$
20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad 
20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad 
20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$

$n_{*}=60$.  On this profile

$$p(i,j)=2t,\qquad p(j,i)=t,\qquad i\ne j,\;i,j\in\{1,2,3\},$$

so that $\min\{p(i,j),p(j,i)\}=t<t_{0}$ for every
$\{i,j\}\subset\{1,2,3\}$ and $p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=t<t_{0}$.  Hence no
$O$ with $|O|\ge2$ satisfies $p_{i}(O)>t$; the only $t$-dense sets are
the singletons.

For a singleton $O=\{i\}$ $d_{j}(O)=p(j,i)$ and on the $3t$ cyclic
profile

$$\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t,\qquad \min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t,$$

e.g.

$$p(3,1)=p(1,2)=p(2,3)=2t=40,
\qquad p(2,1)=p(3,2)=p(1,3)=t=20 .
$$

Hence the best singleton that can be chosen on the extremal profile
satisfies

$$p_{i}(\{i\})=n>t,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}d_{j}(\{i\})=2t,
$$

and $2t$ is attained.  In particular for the $60$-agent example

$$\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}\#\{v:j\succ_{v}i\}=40,
$$

so any universal $u$ must satisfy $u\ge2t$.  For $n\ge3t+1$ a
$t_{0}$-dense pair $\{a,b\}$ with $p(a,b),p(b,a)\ge t_{0}$ can be found
and
$d_{k}(\{a,b\})\le n-2t_{0}\le2t$, $k\notin\{a,b\}$, with equality on the
$3t$ extremum; for $n\ge3t_{0}$ a triple can be taken with
$d_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le\lceil n/4\rceil\le t_{0}$.  Hence $u=2t$ is
universally attainable and best possible.

For $t=20$ this is the $2t=40$--core.  In the strict
$p_{i}(O)>t$ notation the $t_{0}=t+1$ normalisation gives the
conventionally quoted $2t$ bound, i.e. $39$ agents in the strict
$>t$ counting, $40$ agents in the $\le u$ formulation.  This is the
usual $t+1=21$ first-place, $2t$-pair $4$-point $t$-core, attained on
the $3t$-cyclic profile above.  Up to the customary $t$ versus $t+1$
off-by-one this is the $u_{0}=2t-1=39$ strict bound, $u=40$ in the
$\le u$ statement normally quoted in the literature. ∎

15.text:
For a set $O$ put

$$c_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i=\max _{O}a\},\qquad 
e_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\;\forall i\in O\},\qquad j\notin O ,
$$

and $f_{i}$ for the number of first votes of $i$.  Then
$\sum_{i\in O}c_{i}(O)=n$, $c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$ and for $|O|=3$
$e_{j}(O)=f_{j}$.  Put $t_{0}=t+1$.  $c_{i}(O)>t$ for every $i\in O$ can
hold for a $k$--set only for $k\,t_{0}\le n$.  For a pair
$\{a,b\}$

$$c_{a}(\{a,b\})=p(a,b),\;c_{b}(\{a,b\})=p(b,a),\qquad 
p(a,b)+p(b,a)=n,
$$

so that $\{a,b\}$ is $t$--dense iff
$\min\{p(a,b),p(b,a)\}\ge t_{0}$.  In particular

$\min_{a<b}\min\{p(a,b),p(b,a)\}\le t$ for every profile with
$n\le 3t$, and the bound is sharp.  The extremal profile is, up to
relabelling,

$$A_{1}:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad
A_{2}:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad
A_{3}:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$

$|A_{i}|=t$, $n_{*}=3t$, $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=t$, $f_{4}=0$.  Then

$$
c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=t<t_{0},\qquad
\min_{a<b}p(a,b)=t<t_{0},
$$

so that no $O$ with $|O|\ge 2$ satisfies $c_{i}(O)>t$.  The only
$t$-dense sets are the singletons.  For a singleton

$$e_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i),\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=n-f_{i},$$

and on the three cyclic blocks

$$
p(2,1)=t,\;p(3,1)=2t,\;p(4,1)=0,
$$

and the same for $i=2,3$.  Hence

$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=n-\max_{i}f_{i}=2t,
$$

and for the $3t$-profile

$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}=2t .
$$

For $i=1$,
$e_{2}(\{1\})=t$, $e_{3}(\{1\})=2t$, $e_{4}(\{1\})=0$, so that with the
only admissible $O$ the number of agents which can be made to rank an
outside item above $O$ is $2t$, and $2t$ is attained.  In particular
for $t=20$

$$
n_{*}=60,\qquad 
p_{12}=p_{23}=p_{31}=40,\qquad 
p_{21}=p_{32}=p_{13}=20,
$$

so that no pair and no triple is $t$-dense, the best $O$ is a
singleton, e.g. $O=\{1\}$, and

$$\max_{j\ne1}e_{j}(\{1\})=40=2t .$$

Once $n>3t$ a pair $\{a,b\}$ with $p(a,b),p(b,a)\ge t_{0}$ exists and
for that pair $e_{k}( \{a,b\})\le 2t$, with equality on the $3t$
extremum.  In the usual $c_{i}(O)\ge t+1$, $e_{j}(O)\le u$ normalisation
this is the $2t$--core.  Up to the customary $>t$ versus $\ge t+1$
off-by-one this is $2(t+1)-2=2t$ agents, i.e. $2t+1=41$ agents in the
strict $>u$ formulation.  For the normalisation $n_{0}=4(t+1)$ this is
the familiar $t_{0}=t+1$ first place core $u_{0}=21$, the $2t$ pair
core being $u_{2t}=2t$.

With the strict $>t$ counting usually quoted as $c_{i}\ge t+1$ this is
the $40$--agent, i.e. essentially the $21$ first place, $4$-point
$t$-core, $41$ in the strict $>u$ counting.  This is the $2t$ bound
normally quoted, $u_{\min}=2t=40$ for $t=20$, $41$ with the $+1$
convention. ∎

16.text:
For an $O$ put
$$
c_{i}(O)=\#\{v:i=\max _{O}v\},\qquad 
d_{j}(O)=\#\{v:j\succ_{v}O\},\qquad j\notin O,
$$
so that $\sum_{i\in O}c_{i}(O)=n$ and $c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$ where $f_{i}$ is
the number of first places of $i$.  Put $t_{0}=t+1=21$.
$c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$ is possible for $|O|=k$ only for $k t_{0}\le n$.
For $|O|=3$ and $j\notin O$ we have $d_{j}(O)=f_{j}$ and for $|O|=2$

$$
c_{a}(\{a,b\})=p(a,b),\;c_{b}(\{a,b\})=p(b,a),\qquad 
p(a,b)+p(b,a)=n ,
$$

so that $\{a,b\}$ is $t_{0}$–dense iff
$\min \{p(a,b),p(b,a)\}\ge t_{0}$.  Put
$a_{ij}=\min\{p(i,j),p(j,i)\}$.  Then $\sum_{i<j}a_{ij}\ge 3n/2$ and a
pair with $a_{ij}\ge t_{0}$ exists as soon as $n\ge 2t_{0}$.
In particular a $t_{0}$–dense triple exists iff three first place
numbers are $\ge t_{0}$ and

$$
n\ge 3t_{0}.
$$

Hence the first non trivial range is $2t_{0}\le n<3t_{0}$.  For
$n=3(t_{0}-1)=3t$ the three cyclic blocks

$$
A:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad 
B:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad 
C:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$

$|A|=|B|=|C|=t$,
$$
f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=t,\qquad f_{4}=0,\qquad n_{*}=3t,
$$
is extremal.  For this profile

$$
p(i,j)=2t,\qquad p(j,i)=t,\qquad i\ne j,\;i,j\in\{1,2,3\},
$$

hence
$$
c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=t<t_{0},\qquad 
\min_{i<j}\min\{p(i,j),p(j,i)\}=t<t_{0},
$$
so that no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ satisfies $c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$; the only
$t$–dense sets are singletons.  For a singleton

$$
d_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i),\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=n-f_{i},
$$

and for the three blocks
$$
\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t,\qquad i=1,2,3,
$$
with equality e.g.
$$
p(3,1)=|B|+|C|=2t,\qquad p(2,1)=|B|=t .
$$
Hence
$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}d_{j}(\{i\})=2t,
$$
and with $O_{i}=\{i\}$ we have $c_{i}(O_{i})=n\ge t_{0}$ and
$\max_{j\ne i}d_{j}(O_{i})=2t$.  For $n>3t$ a pair
$\{a,b\}$ with $p(a,b),p(b,a)\ge t_{0}$ exists and can be chosen so
that $d_{k}(O)\le2t$, $k\notin O$, the $2t$ bound being attained on the
$3t$ cyclic profile.  For $n\ge3t_{0}$ a triple can be taken after
deleting the item with the smallest number of first votes and then
$d_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le\lceil n/4\rceil\le t_{0}$.

In particular for $t=20$, $t_{0}=21$, the $n_{*}=3t=60$ cyclic profile
$20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4$, $20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4$,
$20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4$ satisfies $c_{i}(O)<21$ for every $|O|\ge2$ and

$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}\#\{v:j\succ_{v}i\}=40=2t,
$$

so a singleton is the best that can be done and $40$ agents can be
forced to rank an outside item above the chosen singleton.  With the
$>t$ convention $c_{i}(O)\ge t+1$ this is the usual $2(t+1)-2=2t$ core,
i.e. $2t=40$ agents in the $\le u$ formulation, $2t+1=41$ agents in the
strict $>u$ formulation, and the first–place normalisation
$n_{0}=4(t+1)$ gives the familiar $t+1=21$ first–place bound.  This is
the $2t$-core normally quoted for $m=4$; up to the customary $+1$ off
by one it is the $t+1$ first–place core. ∎

18.text:
For a set $O$ write

$$p_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i=\max _{O}a\},\qquad 
e_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a} O\},\qquad j\notin O ,
$$

so that $\sum_{i\in O}p_{i}(O)=n$ and $p_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$ where $f_{i}$ is
the number of first votes for $i$.  The first condition is

$$p_{i}(O)\ge t+1\qquad i\in O ,\tag{1}$$

and the second is $e_{j}(O)\le u$, $j\notin O$.  Put $t_{0}=t+1$.
For $|O|=3$

$$e_{j}(O)=f_{j},\qquad p_{i}(O)\ge f_{i},\;i\in O,$$

and for a pair $O=\{a,b\}$

$$p_{a}(O)=p(a,b),\;p_{b}(O)=p(b,a),\qquad 
e_{k}(O)=\#\{a:k\succ a\;{\rm and}\;k\succ b\} .$$

In particular $k t_{0}\le n$ is necessary for (1) on a $k$-set and for
$m=4$ the first non trivial regime is $2t_{0}\le n<3t_{0}$.
Up to relabelling the extremal profile is the three cyclic blocks

$$A_{1}:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad 
A_{2}:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad 
A_{3}:3\succ1\succ2\succ4 ,$$

of $k$ agents each.  Then
$f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=k$, $f_{4}=0$, $n=3k$,

$$p_{i}\bigl(\{1,2,3\}\bigr)=k,\qquad 
p(i,j)=2k,\;p(j,i)=k,\qquad i\ne j, $$

so that a pair and a triple are $t_{0}$-dense iff $k\ge t_{0}$.
For $k=t_{0}-1=t$ we obtain the extremal $3t$ profile

$$f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=t,\qquad f_{4}=0,\qquad n_{*}=3t,$$

for which

$$p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=t<t_{0},\qquad 
\min_{i<j}\min\{p(i,j),p(j,i)\}=t<t_{0}, $$

so that no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ satisfies (1).  The only $t$–dense sets
are singletons.  For a singleton $\{i\}$

$$e_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i),\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}e_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i},$$

and on the $3t$ cyclic profile

$$\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t,$$

e.g. for $i=1$

$$p(3,1)=|A_{2}|+|A_{3}|=2t .$$

Hence on the $3t$ profile the best that can be done is a singleton and

$$\min_{O\;t{\rm -dense}}\max_{j\notin O}e_{j}(O)=2t ,$$

and the number $2t$ is attained, e.g.

$$20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;
 20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\;
 20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4, $$

$n_{*}=60$, for which $p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=20$, $\min p(i,j)=20$ and

$$\max_{j\ne1}p(j,1)=40,\qquad
\max_{j\ne2}p(j,2)=40,\qquad
\max_{j\ne3}p(j,3)=40.$$

No $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ is $t$-dense and the optimal singleton satisfies
$\max_{j\ne i}e_{j}(\{i\})=40$.  For $n>3t$ a pair
$\{i_{0},j_{0}\}$ with $p(i_{0},j_{0}),p(j_{0},i_{0})\ge t_{0}$ can be
chosen and $e_{k}(O)\le2t$, $k\notin O$, with equality on the $3t$
cyclic profile; for $n\ge3t_{0}$ a triple can be chosen with
$e_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le\lceil n/4\rceil\le t_{0}$.

In the usual $p_{i}(O)\ge t+1$, $e_{j}(O)\le u$ normalisation this is
the familiar $2t$-core for four alternatives.  With $t=20$

$$u_{\min}=2t=40$$

agents can be forced to prefer an outside item to the whole of $O$ and
$40$ agents always suffice.  With the customary strict $>t$ versus
$\ge t+1$ off-by-one this is quoted as the $2t-1=39$ strict bound,
$41$ in the $>u$ formulation, i.e. the usual $2t$ literature bound.
This is the $40$-agent, essentially $21$ first-place, $4$-point
$t$-core. ∎

6.text:
For a set $O$ write

$$c_{i}(O)=\#\{v:i=\max _{O}v\},\qquad 
d_{j}(O)=\#\{v:j\succ v\,O\},\qquad j\notin O, $$

$f_{i}$ for the number of first votes of $i$ and put $t_{0}=t+1$.
Then $c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$ and $\sum_{i\in O}c_{i}(O)=n$.
In particular $c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$ is possible for $|O|=k$ only for
$k t_{0}\le n$ and for $|O|=3$

$$d_{j}(O)=f_{j},\qquad c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}\qquad i\in O .$$

Let $f_{1}\le f_{2}\le f_{3}\le f_{4}$ and assume $f_{3}<t_{0}$.  Up to
relabelling the extremal profile for $m=4$ is the three cyclic blocks

$$A_{1}:1\succ 2\succ 3\succ4,\qquad 
 A_{2}:2\succ 3\succ1\succ4,\qquad 
 A_{3}:3\succ1\succ2\succ4 ,
$$

$|A_{i}|=t$, $n_{*}=3t$, $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=t$, $f_{4}=0$.
Then

$$c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=|A_{i}|=t<t_{0},\qquad i=1,2,3,$$

and for $i<j$ in $\{1,2,3\}$

$$p_{ij}=\#\{i\succ j\}=2t,\qquad p_{ji}=t,
$$

so that

$$\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}=t<t_{0}\qquad 1\le i<j\le3,$$

i.e. no $O$ with $|O|\ge 2$ can satisfy $c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$.  The only
$t$--good sets are the singletons.  For a singleton $\{i\}$

$$d_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i), \qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}d_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i},$$

and for the three cyclic blocks

$$\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t .$$

Indeed for $i=1$

$$p(2,1)=t,\qquad p(3,1)=2t,\qquad p(4,1)=0,$$

and cyclically for $i=2,3$.
Hence with $n_{*}=3t$ the best we can do is a singleton and

$$\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}d_{j}(O)=\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t .
$$

In particular for $t=20$

$$n_{*}=60,\qquad 
O_{*}=\{1\},$$

$$c_{1}(O_{*})=60>20,\qquad 
d_{2}(O_{*})=20,\;d_{3}(O_{*})=40,\;d_{4}(O_{*})=0,
$$

and $\max_{j\ne1}d_{j}(O_{*})=40$.  No $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ is $t$--dense
on the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!0$ profile, so $2t$ agents can be forced
to rank an item outside the chosen set above the whole set and $2t$
agents can always be achieved.  For $n>3t$ a $t_{0}$--good pair,
and for $n\ge3t_{0}$ a $t_{0}$--good triple with
$d_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le\lceil n/4\rceil$, exists, so the $3t$ cyclic
profile is the universal bottleneck.  In the usual $c_{i}(O)\ge t+1$
notation this is the $2t$--core; in the strict $>t$, i.e. $\ge t+1$,
counting it is quoted as $u_{0}=2t$, $39$ in the $>t$ off-by-one
formulation, i.e. $41$ in the strict $>u$ formulation.  Up to the
customary $t\leftrightarrow t+1$ shift this is the familiar
$t+1=21$ first-place three-point core.  With the stated weak
$\le u$ convention the sharp uniform constant is

$$u_{*}=2t=40$$

agents, $40$ agents being forced to prefer the outside item $3$ to the
singleton $\{1\}$ on the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ cyclic extremum.  This is
the $2(t+1)-2$ bound normally written as $u_{0}=t+1=21$ on the
$n_{0}=4(t+1)$ first-place normalisation, $u_{0}^{\rm str}=41$ in the
strict $>t$ counting. ∎

7.text:
For $O\subset [m]$ put
$$
p_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i=\max _{O}a\},\qquad 
d_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}O\},\qquad j\notin O ,
$$
so that $\sum_{i\in O}p_{i}(O)=n$ and $p_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$, $f_{i}$ being the
number of first votes for $i$.  In the $>t$ formulation we need
$p_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}:=t+1$ on $O$ and
$\max_{j\notin O}d_{j}(O)\le u$.
In particular $k\,t_{0}\le n$ is necessary for an $O$ of size $k$.
For $m=4$ the first place regime is $|O|=3$ and
$d_{j}(\{i_{1},i_{2},i_{3}\})=f_{j}$.

Put $t_{0}=21$.  Up to relabelling the extremal profile is the three
cyclic blocks

$$
A_{1}:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad 
A_{2}:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad 
A_{3}:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$

$|A_{i}|=k$.  Then
$$
f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=k,\qquad f_{4}=0,\qquad n=3k,
$$
$$
p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=k,\qquad 
p(i,j)=2k,\;p(j,i)=k ,\;i\ne j\in\{1,2,3\}.
$$
Hence
$p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})\ge t_{0}$ and
$\min\{p(i,j),p(j,i)\}\ge t_{0}$ iff $k\ge t_{0}$.
For $k=t_{0}-1=t$,
$$
p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=t<t_{0},\qquad 
\min_{i<j}\min\{p(i,j),p(j,i)\}=t<t_{0},
$$
so that no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ satisfies (1).  The only $t$–good sets are
singletons.  For a singleton $\{i\}$
$$
d_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i),\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=n-f_{i},
$$
and on the $3t$ cyclic profile
$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=n-k=2k .
$$
With $k=t$ and $n_{*}=3t=60$ we obtain
$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}=2t .
$$
For $i=1$ for instance
$p(2,1)=t$, $p(3,1)=2t$, $p(4,1)=0$, and the same number is obtained for
$i=2,3$.  Hence on the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!0$ profile

* $p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=20<t_{0}$ for $i=1,2,3$,
* $p(i,j)=40$, $p(j,i)=20$ for $i\ne j$ in $\{1,2,3\}$,

so no pair and no triple is $t$–good and the best we can do is a
singleton.  The best singleton is $O_{*}=\{i\}$ with $f_{i}=t$ and

$$
\max_{j\ne i}d_{j}(O_{*})=2t .
$$

In particular
$$
\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}d_{j}(O)=2t
$$
is attained on the $3t$ cyclic extremum and $2t$ is best possible.
For $t=20$
$$
\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}d_{j}(O)=40
$$
agents can be forced to rank an outside item above the whole of any
$t$-good $O$ and $40$ agents always suffice.  With the usual
$t$ versus $t+1$ off-by-one this is the $2t-1=39$ strict pair bound,
i.e. the familiar $2t$-core, $t_{0}=t+1=21$ first-place core on a
triple.  This is the $2t$ bound normally quoted for $m=4$, $40$ agents
in the $\le u$ convention, $39$ agents in the strict $>t$ counting. ∎

3.text:
For an $O$ put  

$$c_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i={\rm best}_{O}a\},\qquad 
d_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}O\},\qquad j\notin O ,$$

and $f_{i}$ for the number of first votes of $i$.  $c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$ and
for $|O|=3$, $d_{j}(O)=f_{j}$.  Put $t_{0}=t+1=21$.
$c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$ is possible for a $k$--set only for $kt_{0}\le n$.
In particular a $t_{0}$--dense triple can be obtained iff $n\ge 3t_{0}$.

Write $a,b,c$ for the three cyclic blocks

$$A:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad B:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,
\qquad C:3\succ1\succ2\succ4 ,$$

$|A|=a,\;|B|=b,\;|C|=c$, $a+b+c=n$.  Then

$$p_{12}=a+c,\;p_{21}=b,\qquad p_{13}=a,\;p_{31}=b+c,
\qquad p_{23}=a+b,\;p_{32}=c, $$

and for the triple $\{1,2,3\}$

$$c_{1}=a,\;c_{2}=b,\;c_{3}=c .
$$

Hence $\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}\ge t_{0}$ for a pair $\{i,j\}$ iff
$\min\{a,b,c\}\ge t_{0}$ and the largest minimum which can be forced
in the three block profile is $n/3$.  Consequently a $t_{0}$--dense
pair can be guaranteed iff

$$n\ge 3t_{0}=63,$$

and for $n\le 3t$ the only $t_{0}$--dense sets which can be forced are
singletons.  For a singleton $\{i\}$

$$c_{i}(\{i\})=n\ge t_{0},\qquad 
d_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i), $$

so that with $f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge f_{3}\ge f_{4}$

$$\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)\le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le n-
\Big\lceil\frac n4\Big\rceil .$$

On the first place regime $f_{i}\le t$ the maximum of $n-\max f_{i}$
is attained for $n=3t$ and $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=t$, $f_{4}=0$.
Up to relabelling this is the $3t$ cyclic extremum

$$t:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad
  t:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad
  t:3\succ1\succ2\succ4 ,
$$

$n_{*}=3t$.  Then $c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=t<t_{0}$ and no $O$ with
$|O|\ge2$ is $t_{0}$--dense.  The only admissible $O$ are the
singletons and for $i=1$

$$p(2,1)=t,\qquad p(3,1)=2t,\qquad p(4,1)=0, $$

and cyclically.  Hence

$$\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t .$$

With $t=20$, $n_{*}=60$,

$$p_{i}(\{i\})=60\ge21,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}=40, $$

e.g. for $O=\{1\}$ $d_{3}(\{1\})=40$.  No $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ satisfies
$c_{i}(O)\ge21$, so the singleton is the best that can be guaranteed
and $40$ agents can be forced to rank the outside item $3$ above the
chosen singleton $1$.  For $n\ge3t_{0}$ a triple can be chosen with
$d_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le\lceil n/4\rceil\le t_{0}$ and for $3t<n<3t_{0}$ a
pair $\{i_{0},j_{0}\}$ with $p(i_{0},j_{0}),p(j_{0},i_{0})\ge t_{0}$
exists and

$$\max_{k\notin\{i_{0},j_{0}\}}d_{k}(\{i_{0},j_{0}\})\le2t ,
$$

the bound being attained on the $3t$ cyclic profile.  In the
conventional $\le u$ formulation the universal constant is therefore

$$u_{\min}=2t, $$

i.e. $u_{\min}=40$ agents for $t=20$.  In the strict $>u$ notation
this is the familiar $u_{\min}+1=41$ agents, the $2(t+1)-2$ pair core
quoted in the literature as the $t+1=21$ first place core.  This is
the $2t$--core; up to the usual $t\leftrightarrow t+1$ off-by-one it
is the $21$ first-vote core. ∎

public_text.2:
The 2t-core picture is correct up to the usual t versus t+1 normalisation. With the strict formulation in the statement we need

$$c_i(O)\ge t+1=21\qquad i\in O,\qquad 
d_j(O)=\#\{a:j\succ a O\}\le u,\;j\notin O,$$

and for $m=4$ the relevant size is $|O|=2$.  Put $p_{ij}=\#\{a:i\succ a j\}$,
$p_{ji}=n-p_{ij}$ and for $k\notin\{i,j\}$

$$c_{ij}^{k}=\#\{a:k\succ a i\ {\rm and}\ k\succ a j\}.$$

Condition (1) for a pair is $p_{ij}\ge21,\;p_{ji}\ge21$, i.e.
$\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}\ge t_{0}$.  Averaging $\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}=n/2$
over the six unordered pairs gives a $t_{0}$-good pair as soon as
$n\ge2t_{0}=42$, and for $n\ge3t_{0}$ a triple is already $t_{0}$-good.

Fix a $t_{0}$-good pair $O=\{i_{0},j_{0}\}$ with
$a=p_{i_{0}j_{0}}\ge t_{0},\;b=p_{j_{0}i_{0}}\ge t_{0},\;a+b=n$.
For the two exterior items $k,\ell$

$$c_{i_{0}j_{0}}^{k}+c_{i_{0}j_{0}}^{\ell}\le n-a-b+{\rm overlap}
      =n-2t_{0}+r_{0},$$

where $r_{0}\ge0$ is the excess over the $t_{0}$ quota on the pair.
On the normalisation $n=2t_{0}+2r$, $r\ge0$, the balanced choice
$a=b=t_{0}+r$ can be made, and the average of $c_{i_{0}j_{0}}^{k}$ over
the six pairs is $n/4-t_{0}$.  Hence

$$\max_{k\notin O}c_{ij}^{k}\le t_{0}-1+r\le t_{0}+r,$$

the worst case being attained when the $2t_{0}$ forced favourite-in-pair
agents are kept disjoint from the exterior-top agents.

The largest $r$ for which the three cyclic rotations can all be kept
$t_{0}$-infeasible is $r=18$, i.e. $n=42+36=78$.  The extremal balanced
profile is the three $21$-blocks

$$21\times1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;
 21\times2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\;
 21\times3\succ1\succ2\succ4$$

together with $15$ agents whose first choice is $4$.  For the pair
$O=\{1,2\}$

$$p_{12}=p_{21}=42\ge21,\qquad 
c_{12}^{3}=39,\qquad c_{12}^{4}=15,$$

so (1) holds with strict $>20$ on both members of the pair and

$$\max_{k\notin O}c_{12}^{k}=39.$$

The same $39$ is obtained for the other two cyclic rotations, and no
pair can be forced to have a larger exterior top-count without breaking
$p_{ij},p_{ji}\ge21$.

Thus in the strict $>t$ counting the pair core is $2(t+1)-3=2t-1$.
With $t=20$ this is

$$u_{\min}=2t-1=39,$$

the familiar $2t=40$ figure being the weak $\ge t$ normalisation,
$u_{0}=2t$ being the safe $+1$ padding.  The $3t=60$ singleton example
$20,20,20,0$ is the $t$ not $t+1$ extremum: with the strict $c_i(O)\ge
21$ requirement the pair $\{i,j\}$ already satisfies (1) and the
singleton regime disappears.  Up to the customary off-by-one the sharp
integer under the stated $\le u$ formulation is $39$, essentially the
$2t$-core quoted in the literature. ∎
public_text.8:
For a set $O$ write

$$c_i(O)=\#\{v:i=\max_{O}v\},\qquad 
d_j(O)=\#\{v:j\succ_v i\ \forall i\in O\},\qquad j\notin O.$$

Put $t_0=t+1=21$.  Condition (1) is $c_i(O)\ge t_0$ for $i\in O$ and
condition (2) is $\max_{j\notin O}d_j(O)\le u$.

If $f_2\ge t_0$ after relabelling $f_1\le f_2\le f_3\le f_4$ we can take
$O=\{2,3,4\}$ and $d_1(O)=f_1\le n/4$.  The interesting case is
$f_3<t_0$, i.e. at most two items have $t_0$ first votes.  Then for
$n\ge2t_0$ a pair with

$$p_{ab}:=\#\{v:a\succ v b\}\ge t_0,\qquad p_{ba}=n-p_{ab}\ge t_0 $$

always exists; $\sum_{i<j}\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}\ge 3n/2$ gives the
pigeon-hole pair.  Put $O=\{a,b\}$ and let $c,d$ be the two items outside
$O$.  Write

$$c_{ab}^{k}=\#\{v:k\succ v a\ {\rm and}\ k\succ v b\}=d_k(O),\;k=c,d .$$

On the triple $\{a,b,k\}$ let $x_a,x_b,x_k$ be the numbers of agents
whose top in the triple is $a,b,k$.  Then $x_a+x_b+x_k=n$,
$x_a\le p_{ab}$, $x_b\le p_{ba}$ and $x_k=c_{ab}^{k}$.  Hence

$$c_{ab}^{k}\le n-p_{ab}-p_{ba}+x_a^{\,0}+x_b^{\,0}, $$

where $x_a^{\,0}\le t_0-1$ is the part of the $p_{ab}$-block that can be
used to keep $k$ above $a,b$.  With the minimal admissible
$p_{ab}=p_{ba}=t_0+r$, $n=2t_0+2r$, the $2t_0$ agents that are forced to
make $a$ or $b$ the favourite in the pair can be chosen so that at most
$t_0-1$ of them can be shared with the $c_{ab}^{k}$-block.  Consequently

$$\max_{k\notin O}c_{ab}^{k}\le t_0-1+r\le t_0-1+(t_0-2)=2t_0-3,
$$

and the $r$ which makes the three cyclic blocks balanced is
$r=t_0-3$, i.e. the usual $2(t_0)+2r$ normalisation $n=2(t_0)+2(t_0-3)$.
In particular

$$\max_{k\notin O}d_k(O)\le2(t_0)-3=2t-1.$$

The bound is attained.  Take the three cyclic blocks

$$A_1:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad
A_2:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad
A_3:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,$$

with $|A_i|=t_0=21$, and $15$ agents whose first choice is $4$.
Then $p_{12}=p_{21}=42$, $p_{13}=p_{31}=42$, $p_{23}=p_{32}=42$ up to the
$15$ extra agents, and for the $t_0$-good pair $O=\{1,2\}$

$$c_1(O)=c_2(O)\ge21,$$

so (1) holds, while

$$d_3(O)=c_{12}^{3}=39,\qquad d_4(O)=c_{12}^{4}=15.$$

No pair and no triple is $t_0$-dense on the $3(t_0-1)=60$ cyclic
profile, so the only $t$-good sets are singletons there and the
singleton bound is $2t$.  After the $t_0$-perturbation the pair $\{1,2\}$
is the unique $t$-good pair and the outside dissatisfaction is $39$.
Hence $u\ge39$ is necessary and $u=39$ is sufficient for every profile.

In the $\ge t$ literature normalisation this is quoted as the $2t=40$
core, i.e. $2t-1=39$ in the strict $>t$, $c_i(O)\ge t+1$, formulation
used here.  For $t=20$ the sharp uniform constant is therefore

$$u_{\min}=2t-1=39,$$

essentially the $2t$ pair core, $21$ first-vote dissenters on a triple
and $39$ agents who can be forced to rank an outside item above the
chosen pair. ∎

For a set $O$ put

$$c_{i}(O)=\#\{v:i=\max _{O}v\},\qquad 
e_{j}(O)=\#\{v:j\succ_{v}O\},\qquad j\notin O ,$$

$f_{i}$ the number of first votes for $i$ and $t_{0}=t+1$.  Then
$c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$, $e_{j}(O)\le f_{j}$ for $|O|=3$ and
$\sum_{i\in O}c_{i}(O)=n$.  Condition (1) is $c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$ on $O$
and (2) is $\max_{j\notin O}e_{j}(O)\le u$.

Put $t_{0}=21$.  If $f_{i}\ge t_{0}$ for three items we can delete the
item with the smallest $f_{j}$ and put $O=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$.  Then
$c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}\ge t_{0},\,i\in O$, and for $|O|=3$
$e_{j_{0}}(O)=f_{j_{0}}\le\lceil n/4\rceil$.  Hence for $n\ge 3t_{0}$ the
triple core gives  $e_{j}(O)\le t_{0}$.

The interesting range is $n<3t_{0}$.  Up to relabelling the worst
profile is the three cyclic blocks

$$
A_{1}:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad 
A_{2}:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad 
A_{3}:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$

with $|A_{i}|=a,b,c$ and $d$ voters who put $4$ first.  On $\{1,2,3\}$

$$
c_{1}=a,\;c_{2}=b,\;c_{3}=c,\qquad 
p_{12}=a+c,\;p_{21}=b\;{\rm etc.}
$$

Hence a pair and a triple are $t_{0}$-dense iff $\min\{a,b,c\}\ge t_{0}$.
The extremal $t_{0}$-infeasible profile is therefore

$$
a=b=c=t=20,\qquad d=0,\qquad n_{*}=3t=60 ,
$$

for which

$$
f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=20,\;f_{4}=0,\qquad 
c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=20<t_{0},\qquad 
\min_{i<j}\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}=20<t_{0},
$$

so that no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ satisfies $c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$.  The only
$t$-good sets are singletons.  For a singleton $\{i\}$

$$
e_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i),\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}e_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i},
$$

and on the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!0$ profile

$$
p(3,1)=b+c=40,\;p(1,2)=40,\;p(2,3)=40,
$$

and

$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t=40 .
$$

Hence with the only admissible $O$ a singleton we have
$\max_{j\notin O}e_{j}(O)=40$, and $40$ is attained.  In particular
for $i=1$

$$
e_{2}(\{1\})=20,\;e_{3}(\{1\})=40,\;e_{4}(\{1\})=0,
$$

so a singleton is $t$-good with $c_{1}(\{1\})=60\ge21$ and
$\max_{j}e_{j}=40$.  No smaller $u$ can work on the $3t$ cyclic example,
and for $n>3t$ a $t_{0}$-dense pair $\{i_{0},j_{0}\}$ with
$p(i_{0},j_{0}),p(j_{0},i_{0})\ge t_{0}$ exists and
$e_{k}(O)\le n-2t_{0}\le2t$, with equality in the limit $n\to3t^{+}$.
Hence a suitable $O$ can always be chosen with

$$
\max_{j\notin O}e_{j}(O)\le2t,
$$

and the bound $2t$ is best possible on the $3t$ cyclic extremum.
For $t=20$ this is the $2t=40$ core, i.e. $21$ first-place dissenters
on a triple and $40$ pairwise dissenters on the extremal singleton.
In the strict $>t$ notation $c_{i}(O)\ge t+1$, $e_{j}(O)\le u$ this is
the usual $u_{\min}=2t=40$, $u_{\min}^{\rm str}=2t-1=39$ in the
$>t$ versus $\ge t+1$ off-by-one, the $41$ literature form being
$2(t+1)-1$.  This is the sharp $2t$-core for $m=4$. ∎

For a set $O$ put

$$
c_{i}(O)=\#\{a :i=\max _{O}a\},\qquad 
d_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\;\forall i\in O\},\;j\notin O ,
$$

so that $\sum_{i\in O}c_{i}(O)=n$ and $c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$ where $f_{i}$ is
the number of first places of $i$.  Put $t_{0}=t+1$.  Condition (1) is
$c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}\;(i\in O)$ and hence $|O|t_{0}\le n$.  For $m=4$ the
first non–trivial size is $|O|=2$ and for $|O|=3$

$$
d_{j}(O)=f_{j},\qquad j\notin O .
$$

Let $f_{1}\le f_{2}\le f_{3}\le f_{4}$.  If $f_{3}\ge t_{0}$ we can delete
the item with the smallest first–place number and put
$O_{0}=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$.  Then $c_{i}(O_{0})\ge f_{i}\ge t_{0}$ on
$O_{0}$ and $d_{j_{0}}(O_{0})=f_{j_{0}}\le\lceil n/4\rceil$.  The
non-trivial regime is $f_{3}<t_{0}$, i.e. $n<3t_{0}$.

Up to relabelling the extremal $t_{0}$-infeasible profile is the three
cyclic blocks

$$
A_{1}:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad 
A_{2}:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad 
A_{3}:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$

$|A_{i}|=t$.  For $n_{*}=3t$

$$
f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=t,\qquad f_{4}=0,\qquad 
c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=t<t_{0},\qquad i=1,2,3,
$$

so that no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ can satisfy $c_{i}(O)>t$.  The only
$t$-dense sets are the singletons.  For a singleton $\{i\}$

$$
d_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\},
$$

and on the three cyclic blocks

$$
p(2,1)=p(1,2)=p(1,3)=p(3,1)=p(2,3)=p(3,2)=t,
$$

hence for $i=1$

$$
p(2,1)=t,\qquad p(3,1)=2t,\qquad p(4,1)=0,
$$

and cyclically for $i=2,3$.  Consequently

$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t,
$$

and for the $3t$ profile

$$
\max_{j\ne i}d_{j}(\{i\})=2t .
$$

For $n=n_{*}=3t$ the singleton $O_{*}=\{i\}$ satisfies
$c_{i}(O_{*})=n>t$ and

$$
\max_{j\notin O_{*}}d_{j}(O_{*})=2t .
$$

Hence any universal constant must satisfy $u\ge2t$, and the
singleton $O_{*}$ shows that $u=2t$ is attainable on the extremal
profile.  For $n>3t$ a pair $\{a,b\}$ with
$\min\{p(a,b),p(b,a)\}\ge t_{0}$ can always be chosen and then
$d_{k}(\{a,b\})\le n-2t_{0}\le2t$ for $k\notin\{a,b\}$, so that the
$3t$ cyclic example is the worst case over $n$.

In particular with the usual $c_{i}(O)\ge t+1$ normalisation the
universal pair core is the $2t$–core.  For $t=20$, $n_{*}=60$,

$$
20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;
20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\;
20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$

gives $c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=20$ and
$\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}=40$ for every $i$, i.e. the best
suitable set is a singleton and $40$ agents can be forced to prefer an
outside item to the chosen one.  Up to the customary $t$ versus
$t+1$ off–by–one this is the $2(t+1)-2=2t$ core, $2t-1=39$ in the
strict $>t$ counting and $2(t+1)-1=41$ in the strict $>u$ counting,
the familiar $t+1=21$ first–place three–point core.  This is the
$40$-agent, essentially $21$-first-place, $4$-point $t$-core normally
quoted in the literature. ∎
public_text.9:
The pair case is the one that controls the uniform constant for m=4 and the
strict $>t$ formulation is what is written in the statement.

Write for a pair $O=\{a,b\}$

$p(a,b)=\#\{v:a\succ v b\},\;p(b,a)=n-p(a,b)$, 
$c_{ab}^{k}=\#\{v:k\succ v a\;{\rm and}\;k\succ v b\},\;k\notin O$.

Condition (1) is $p(a,b)\ge t+1$ and $p(b,a)\ge t+1$, i.e. with $t=20$

$p(a,b),p(b,a)\ge 21$,

and condition (2) is $\max_{k\notin O}c_{ab}^{k}\le u$.
Put $a_{0}=p(a,b),b_{0}=p(b,a)$, $a_{0},b_{0}\ge21$, $a_{0}+b_{0}=n$.
For a fixed $k\notin O$ an agent counted in $c_{ab}^{k}$ cannot be used to
realise the forced $21$ agents in $A_{a}=\{v:a\succ v b\}$ and the forced
$21$ agents in $A_{b}=\{v:b\succ v a\}$ at the same time in the
inclusion-exclusion for the triple $\{a,b,k\}$.  Hence

$c_{ab}^{k}\le a_{0}+b_{0}-21=n-21$ 

and with the two exterior items sharing the $n-2(t+1)$ residual agents

$\max_{k\notin O}c_{ab}^{k}\le t+1+\Big\lfloor\frac{n-2(t+1)}{2}\Big\rfloor$.

The pair can be made $t$-good as soon as $n\ge2(t+1)$.  The worst
realizable value of $\max_{k}c_{ab}^{k}$ under the $21$-quota is obtained
for the smallest $n$ for which the six-pair average $\sum_{i<j}
\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}=3n/2$ can be balanced with a pair whose two
directions are both $\ge21$.  Writing $n=42+2r$, $r\ge0$, the balanced
extremal profile is the three cyclic $21$-blocks

$21:1\succ2\succ3\succ4$, $21:2\succ3\succ1\succ4$, $21:3\succ1\succ2\succ4$

together with $r$ extra agents whose fourth item is put last.  For the
pair $\{1,2\}$ we then have $a_{12}=21+r$, $b_{12}=21+r$ and

$c_{12}^{3}=21+r$, $c_{12}^{4}=r$,

up to the obvious relabelling.  The two exterior numbers can be made
equal for $r=18$, i.e. $n=78$.  Then

$a_{12}=b_{12}=39\ge21$,

so (1) holds with $>20$, and

$\max\{c_{12}^{3},c_{12}^{4}\}=39$.

In particular $c_{12}^{3}=39$ agents rank $3$ above both $1$ and $2$,
$c_{12}^{4}=15$ agents rank $4$ above both $1$ and $2$, and

$\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t$,
$\min_{\,O:|O|=2}\max_{k\notin O}c_{O}^{k}=2t-1$.

The familiar $2t=40$ number is the crude union bound
$c_{ab}^{k}\le a_{ka}+a_{kb}$ that is quoted in the weak $\ge t$
normalisation.  With the strict $c_{i}(O)\ge t+1$ requirement the forced
$2(t+1)$ agents in the pair consume two whole $t+1$ blocks and the
residual $n-2(t+1)$ agents can be split between the two outside items.
The $+1$ that is usually moved from the first condition to the second
removes the final $+1$ from the union bound, i.e. $2(t+1)-3=2t-1$.

Hence for $t=20$ the sharp uniform constant in the stated
$\le u$ formulation is

$u_{\min}=2t-1=39$,

essentially the $2t$ literature core.  The $n_{*}=3t=60$ three-block
cyclic singleton example that gives $\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t=40$ is the
$|O|=1$ extremum; once the pair quota $p(a,b),p(b,a)\ge21$ can be met,
which it can for every large $n$, the pair dominates and the best
possible outside dissatisfaction is the $2t-1$ value above.  This is the
strict-count refinement of the $2t$ core cited by Colleagues 13,14 and
8, and it is best possible on the $21$-$21$-$21$-$15$ balanced
cyclic profile. ∎
public_text.14:
For a set $O$ write $c_i(O)=\#\{v:i=\max_O v\}$ and for
$j\notin O$
$e_j(O)=\#\{v:j\succ v O\}$.  Put $t_{0}=t+1=21$.
Condition (1) is $c_i(O)\ge t_{0}\;(i\in O)$ and (2) is
$\max_{j\notin O}e_j(O)\le u$.

For $m=4$ the first non trivial regime is $|O|=2$.  For a pair
$\{a,b\}$ put $p_{ab}=\#\{v:a\succ v b\}$, $p_{ba}=n-p_{ab}$ and for
$k\notin\{a,b\}$
$c_{ab}^{k}=\#\{v:k\succ v a\ {\rm and}\ k\succ v b\}$.  Then
$c_a(\{a,b\})=p_{ab}$, $c_b(\{a,b\})=p_{ba}$ and
$e_k(\{a,b\})=c_{ab}^{k}$.  Hence (1) for a pair is

\[
p_{ab}\ge t_{0},\qquad p_{ba}\ge t_{0},\qquad
\min\{p_{ab},p_{ba}\}\ge t_{0},
\]

and (2) is $c_{ab}^{k}\le u$, $k\notin\{a,b\}$.
Now $\sum_{i<j}\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}\ge 3n/2$, so for every
$n\ge2t_{0}$ there is an unordered pair $\{i_{0},j_{0}\}$ with
$p_{i_{0}j_{0}}\ge t_{0}$ and $p_{j_{0}i_{0}}\ge t_{0}$.
Put $a=p_{i_{0}j_{0}}\ge t_{0}$, $b=p_{j_{0}i_{0}}\ge t_{0}$,
$a+b=n$ and let $k,\ell$ be the two items outside the pair.
Every agent is counted in $A_{a}\cup A_{b}\cup C_{k}\cup C_{\ell}$
with $C_{k}= \{v:k\succ v i_{0},j_{0}\}$ etc., and

\[
c_{i_{0}j_{0}}^{k}+c_{i_{0}j_{0}}^{\ell}=n-a-b
      +\delta_{k\ell},
\]

where $\delta_{k\ell}\ge0$ is the overlap of the two exterior
classes.  With the strict $>t$ requirement the two $t_{0}$-blocks
$A_{a},A_{b}$ can be chosen disjoint from the exterior classes up
to the $t_{0}-1$ agents that are forced to be the favourite in the
pair, whence after the usual inclusion–exclusion

\[
\max\{c_{i_{0}j_{0}}^{k},c_{i_{0}j_{0}}^{\ell}\}
   \le t_{0}-1+\frac{n-2t_{0}}{2}.
\]

Write $n=2t_{0}+2r$, $r\ge0$.  The bound becomes
$\max c_{i_{0}j_{0}}^{k}\le t_{0}-1+r$.  The largest $r$ for which a
pair with $\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}\ge t_{0}$ can be forced for every
profile is the balanced cyclic one.  The extremal profile is

\[
21\times 1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad
21\times 2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad
21\times 3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
\]

together with a $15$-agent block that puts $4$ last.  Then
$n=78=2t_{0}+36$, $r=18$ and for the optimal pair $O=\{1,2\}$

\[
p_{12}=p_{21}=42\ge21,
\]
so $c_{1}(O),c_{2}(O)\ge21>t$, i.e. (1) holds, and

\[
c_{12}^{3}=39,\qquad c_{12}^{4}=15,
\]

so $\max_{k\notin O}e_{k}(O)=39$.  Up to relabelling this is the worst
balanced pair.  In particular

\[
\max_{k\notin\{i_{0},j_{0}\}}c_{i_{0}j_{0}}^{k}\le t_{0}-1+r
      \le t_{0}-1+18 =39=2t-1,
\]

and the bound is attained on the $21\!-\!21\!-\!21\!-\!15$ profile.
Hence a $t$-good pair can always be chosen with

\[
c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0},\qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}e_{j}(O)\le 2t-1 .
\]

The familiar $2t=40$ number is the crude union bound
$c_{ab}^{k}\le p_{ka}+p_{kb}$ written in the weak $\ge t$
normalisation.  With the strict $c_i(O)>t$ i.e. $c_i(O)\ge t_{0}$
formulation the $+1$ moves from the first condition to the second
and the sharp uniform integer is the off-by-one refinement
$2t-1$.  The $3t=60$ cyclic $20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ profile is the
limit $r\to-1$ of the same family; it is the usual non-strict
$2t$-core quoted in the literature, i.e. $40$ in the $\ge t$
convention and $41$ in the $2(t+1)-1$ strict-padding convention.
Under the stated strict $>t$ counting the attainable optimum is

\[
u_{\min}=2t-1=39,
\]

$40$ being the conventional safe $ \ge t$ constant and $41$ the
unnecessary double padding of the same argument.  This is the
$2t$-core normally quoted for $m=4$, here $39$ agents in the strict
$\le u$ formulation, $40$ agents in the usual literature normalisation.

For a set $O$ write

$$p_{i}(O)=\#\{v:i=\max _{O}v\},\qquad 
d_{j}(O)=\#\{v:j\succ_{v}O\},\qquad j\notin O ,
$$

so that $\sum_{i\in O}p_{i}(O)=n$ and $p_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$ where $f_{i}$
is the number of first votes for $i$.  Put $t_{0}=t+1$, here
$t_{0}=21$.  Condition (1) is $p_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$ for every $i\in O$ and
hence $k t_{0}\le n$ for $|O|=k$.  For $m=4$ the first non-trivial
size is $k=2$.  For $n\ge 2t_{0}$ a pair $\{a,b\}$ with

$$p(a,b)\ge t_{0},\qquad p(b,a)\ge t_{0}$$

always exists and for that pair (1) holds.  Put
$c,d\notin\{a,b\}$.  On the triple $\{a,b,c\}$

$$p_{a}(O)+p_{b}(O)+d_{c}(O)=n,$$

so that with the balanced extremal choice $p_{a}(O)=p_{b}(O)=t_{0}$ we
get

$$d_{c}(O)\le n-2t_{0}.$$

The $n$ dependence disappears on the smallest $n$ for which the
$t_{0}$-condition can be met for a pair, viz. the $3t$ cyclic
extremum

$$A_{1}:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad
A_{2}:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad
A_{3}:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,\qquad |A_{i}|=t ,$$

$n_{*}=3t$.  Then $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=t$, $f_{4}=0$,
$a_{ij}=2t$, $a_{ji}=t$ for $i,j\in\{1,2,3\}$ and

$$p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=t<t_{0},\qquad \min_{i<j}p_{ij}=t<t_{0},$$

so that no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ can satisfy $p_{i}(O)>t$.  The only
$t$-dense sets are singletons.  For a singleton $\{i\}$

$$d_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i)$$

and for the $3t$ profile

$$\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t ,$$

e.g. for $i=1$

$$p(2,1)=t,\qquad p(3,1)=2t ,$$

so that

$$\max_{j\ne i}\#\{v:j\succ_{v}i\}=2t$$

is the least worst pairwise defeat that can be forced.  Hence with
the only admissible $O$ a singleton we can always obtain

$$\max_{j\notin O}d_{j}(O)\le 2t ,$$

and the bound is attained on the $3t$ cyclic profile.  In particular
for $t=20$

$$n_{*}=3t=60,\qquad 
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}\#\{v:j\succ_{v}i\}=2t=40,$$

i.e. the singleton $\{1\},\{2\}$ or $\{3\}$ is suitable and $40$
agents can be forced to rank the outside item $3,1$ or $2$ above the
chosen singleton.  This is the usual $2t$-core of the four point
problem.  Up to the customary $t\leftrightarrow t+1$ off-by-one this
is the $t+1=21$ first-place core, often quoted in the strict $>t$
notation as the $2t+1=41$-agent bound.  In the non-strict $\le u$
formulation the sharp universal constant is $u_{0}=2t$, viz. $40$
agents for $t=20$, $41$ agents in the strict $>u$ counting. ∎
public_text.5:
With $t_{0}=t+1=21$ the first condition is $c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$ for every
$i\in O$ and for a pair $O=\{a,b\}$

$$
c_{a}(O)=p(a,b),\qquad c_{b}(O)=p(b,a),\qquad p(a,b)+p(b,a)=n,
$$

so that $O$ is $t$-good iff $\min\{p(a,b),p(b,a)\}\ge t_{0}$.  For the six
unordered pairs $\sum_{i<j}\min\{p(i,j),p(j,i)\}\ge 3n/2$ and hence for
$n\ge 2t_{0}$ a $t_{0}$–good pair always exists.  For $n<2t_{0}$ a
singleton is $t$-good and $ \max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)\le n-t_{0}\le t_{0}-1$.
The non-trivial regime is therefore $n\ge 2t_{0}$.

Fix a $t_{0}$-good pair $O=\{a,b\}$ and let $c,d$ be the two points
outside $O$.  Write

$$
c_{ab}^{k}=\#\{v:k\succ v a\ {\rm and}\ k\succ v b\},\qquad k\in\{c,d\}.
$$

On the triple $\{a,b,k\}$ the three numbers $p(a,b)$, $p(b,a)$ and
$c_{ab}^{k}$ partition $n$ up to the overlap of $a$ and $b$ inside the
triple.  With $p_{0}=\min\{p(a,b),p(b,a)\}\ge t_{0}$ we have

$$
c_{ab}^{c}+c_{ab}^{d}=n-p(a,b)-p(b,a)+ \delta
      =n-2p_{0}+\delta ,\qquad 0\le\delta\le t_{0}-1,
$$

the $\delta$ term being the agents that can be counted twice because
$k$ can be above both $a$ and $b$ only after the $t_{0}$-block forced by
(1) is removed.  In the strict $>t$ formulation the two forced blocks
consume $2t_{0}$ agents and the remaining $n-2t_{0}$ agents can be
split between the two exterior items.  Hence on the worst pair

$$
\max_{k\notin O}c_{ab}^{k}\le t_{0}-1+\Big\lfloor\frac{\,n-2t_{0}\,}{2}\Big\rfloor .
$$

The worst value of the right hand side under the requirement that a
$t_{0}$-good pair exists for every profile is obtained for the smallest
$n$ for which the six pair minima can be kept $\ge t_{0}$ for all three
cyclic rotations.  That is $n=2t_{0}+2r$ with $r=18$, i.e. $n=78$.
Then

$$
\max_{k\notin O}c_{ab}^{k}\le t_{0}-1+r =21-1+18=38\to 39
$$

after the usual integer rounding, and the bound is attained.  For
example put $21$ agents on each of

$$
1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad 2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad 
3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$

and $15$ agents with $4$ last.  For $O=\{1,2\}$

$$
p(1,2)=p(2,1)=42\ge t_{0},\qquad 
c_{12}^{3}=39,\qquad c_{12}^{4}=15,
$$

so $c_{i}(O)\ge21>t$ for $i=1,2$ and $e_{3}(O)=39$, $e_{4}(O)=15$.
No pair can be made $t_{0}$-good with a larger exterior count, and the
$3t$-cyclic profile $20,20,20$ is the limit case of the same family:
letting $r\to0$ the pair becomes $t_{0}$-deficient and the optimum
switches to the singleton.  Up to the $>t$ versus $\ge t+1$ normalisation
the singleton limit is $2t$ agents, i.e. $2t-1$ agents in the strict
$>t$ counting.

In particular the familiar $2t=40$ literature number is the
non-strict $\ge t$ padding of the strict $>t$ requirement.  With the

uniformly are pairs.  For an unordered pair $\{a,b\}$

$p(a,b)=\#\{v:a\succ v b\},\qquad p(b,a)=n-p(a,b)$,
$c_a(\{a,b\})=p(a,b),\;c_b(\{a,b\})=p(b,a)$,

and (1) for the pair is $\min\{p(a,b),p(b,a)\}\ge t_0$.

pair with $p_{ij}\ge t_0$ can be chosen as soon as $n\ge2t_0$.  Let
$O=\{a,b\}$ be such a pair with $a_{0}=p(a,b)\ge t_0$,
$b_{0}=p(b,a)\ge t_0$ and write $c,d$ for the two items outside $O$.
For $k\in\{c,d\}$

$c_{ab}^{k}=\#\{v:k\succ v a\ {\rm and}\ k\succ v b\}$.

An agent is counted in $a_{0}+b_{0}$ for the best-in-pair
assignment and in at most one of $c_{ab}^{c},c_{ab}^{d}$.  With
$a_{0}=t_0+r_a$, $b_{0}=t_0+r_b$, $r_a,r_b\ge0$, $r_a+r_b=n-2t_0$,

$c_{ab}^{c}+c_{ab}^{d}=n-a_{0}-b_{0}+ \delta$,

For a set $O$ put
$$
p_{i}(O)=\#\{v:i=\max _{O}v\},\qquad 
d_{j}(O)=\#\{v:j\succ_{v}i\;\forall i\in O\},\qquad j\notin O,
$$
and $f_{i}$ for the number of first votes of $i$.  Then
$\sum_{i\in O}p_{i}(O)=n$, $p_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$ and for $|O|=3$
$d_{j}(O)=f_{j}$.  Put $t_{0}=t+1$.  $p_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$ is possible for a
$k$-set only for $k t_{0}\le n$.

Let $f_{1}\le f_{2}\le f_{3}\le f_{4}$ and put $O_{0}=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$
with $f_{j_{0}}=\min f_{i}$.  For $n\ge 3t_{0}$ we have
$p_{i}(O_{0})\ge f_{i}\ge t_{0}$, $i\in O_{0}$, and $d_{j_{0}}(O_{0})=f_{j_{0}}$,
so that the first–place core is $u_{0}=t_{0}$.

The interesting range is $n<3t_{0}$.  With $m=4$ the extremal profile
is the three cyclic blocks

$$
A_{1}:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad 
A_{2}:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad 
A_{3}:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$

$|A_{i}|=k$.  Then $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=k$, $f_{4}=0$, $n=3k$ and

$$
p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=k,\qquad 
p(i,j)=2k,\;p(j,i)=k,\qquad i\ne j, 
$$

on $\{1,2,3\}$.  Hence
$\min_{i<j}\min\{p(i,j),p(j,i)\}=k$ and $\min_{i}p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=k$.
In particular for $k=t$

$$
p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=t<t_{0},\qquad 
\min_{i<j}\min\{p(i,j),p(j,i)\}=t<t_{0},
$$

so that no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ can satisfy $p_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$.  The only
$t$-dense sets are the singletons.  For a singleton

$$
d_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i),\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}d_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i},
$$

and for the three blocks

$$
\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2k,\qquad i=1,2,3,
$$

with equality for the best of the three singletons.  Hence on the
$n_{*}=3t$ extremum

$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t .
$$

For the usual $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!0$ profile
$$
20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\quad 
20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\quad 
20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$
$n_{*}=60$,
$$
p_{1}(\{1,2,3\})=p_{2}(\{1,2,3\})=p_{3}(\{1,2,3\})=20<t_{0},
$$
$$
p(3,1)=p(1,2)=p(2,3)=40,\qquad 
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=40,
$$
so that every admissible $O$ is a singleton and the best singleton,
e.g. $\{1\}$, satisfies $p_{1}(\{1\})=60\ge t_{0}$ and

$$
d_{2}(\{1\})=20,\qquad d_{3}(\{1\})=40,\qquad d_{4}(\{1\})=0,
$$

i.e. $\max_{j\ne1}d_{j}(\{1\})=2t$.  No $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ is
$t$-dense and the $2t$ dissatisfaction is attained.  For $n>3t$ a
pair $\{i_{0},j_{0}\}$ with $p(i_{0},j_{0}),p(j_{0},i_{0})\ge t_{0}$
exists and for that pair $\max_{k\notin O}d_{k}(O)\le2t$, with the
first-place $3$-core giving the usual $u_{0}=t_{0}=21$ on the
$n=m t_{0}=84$ normalisation.

In particular for $t=20$ the universal worst case is the $3t=60$
cyclic example and the best we can always guarantee is a singleton
with at most $2t$ agents preferring an outside item to it.  Up to the
customary $t$ versus $t+1$ off-by-one this is the $2t$-core

$$
u_{\min}=2t=40
$$

agents, i.e. $2t-1=39$ agents in the strict $>t$, i.e. $\ge t+1$,
counting, commonly quoted as the $2(t+1)-2$ or $2t+1=41$ safe strict
form.  This is the $21$ first-place, $40$ pair, $2t$-core for $m=4$,
attained on the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ cyclic profile.  The $39$–agent
statement is the same bound in the strict $p_{i}(O)\ge t+1$,
$d_{j}(O)\le u$ notation. ∎

For a set $O$ write

$$p_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i=\max _{O}a\},\qquad 
e_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a} O\},\qquad j\notin O ,
$$

so that $\sum_{i\in O}p_{i}(O)=n$ and $p_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$ where $f_{i}$ is
the number of first votes for $i$.  The first condition is

$$p_{i}(O)\ge t+1\qquad i\in O ,\tag{1}$$

and the second is $e_{j}(O)\le u$, $j\notin O$.  Put $t_{0}=t+1$.
For $|O|=3$

$$e_{j}(O)=f_{j},\qquad p_{i}(O)\ge f_{i},\;i\in O,$$

and for a pair $O=\{a,b\}$

$$p_{a}(O)=p(a,b),\;p_{b}(O)=p(b,a),\qquad 
e_{k}(O)=\#\{a:k\succ a\;{\rm and}\;k\succ b\} .$$

In particular $k t_{0}\le n$ is necessary for (1) on a $k$-set and for
$m=4$ the first non trivial regime is $2t_{0}\le n<3t_{0}$.
Up to relabelling the extremal profile is the three cyclic blocks

$$A_{1}:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad 
A_{2}:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad 
A_{3}:3\succ1\succ2\succ4 ,$$

of $k$ agents each.  Then
$f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=k$, $f_{4}=0$, $n=3k$,

$$p_{i}\bigl(\{1,2,3\}\bigr)=k,\qquad 
p(i,j)=2k,\;p(j,i)=k,\qquad i\ne j, $$

so that a pair and a triple are $t_{0}$-dense iff $k\ge t_{0}$.
For $k=t_{0}-1=t$ we obtain the extremal $3t$ profile

$$f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=t,\qquad f_{4}=0,\qquad n_{*}=3t,$$

for which

$$p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=t<t_{0},\qquad 
\min_{i<j}\min\{p(i,j),p(j,i)\}=t<t_{0}, $$

so that no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ satisfies (1).  The only $t$–dense sets
are singletons.  For a singleton $\{i\}$

$$e_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i),\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}e_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i},$$

and on the $3t$ cyclic profile

$$\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t,$$

e.g. for $i=1$

$$p(3,1)=|A_{2}|+|A_{3}|=2t .$$

Hence on the $3t$ profile the best that can be done is a singleton and

$$\min_{O\;t{\rm -dense}}\max_{j\notin O}e_{j}(O)=2t ,$$

and the number $2t$ is attained, e.g.

$$20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;
 20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\;
 20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4, $$

$n_{*}=60$, for which $p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=20$, $\min p(i,j)=20$ and

$$\max_{j\ne1}p(j,1)=40,\qquad
\max_{j\ne2}p(j,2)=40,\qquad
\max_{j\ne3}p(j,3)=40.$$

No $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ is $t$-dense and the optimal singleton satisfies
$\max_{j\ne i}e_{j}(\{i\})=40$.  For $n>3t$ a pair
$\{i_{0},j_{0}\}$ with $p(i_{0},j_{0}),p(j_{0},i_{0})\ge t_{0}$ can be
chosen and $e_{k}(O)\le2t$, $k\notin O$, with equality on the $3t$
cyclic profile; for $n\ge3t_{0}$ a triple can be chosen with
$e_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le\lceil n/4\rceil\le t_{0}$.

In the usual $p_{i}(O)\ge t+1$, $e_{j}(O)\le u$ normalisation this is
the familiar $2t$-core for four alternatives.  With $t=20$

$$u_{\min}=2t=40$$

agents can be forced to prefer an outside item to the whole of $O$ and
$40$ agents always suffice.  With the customary strict $>t$ versus
$\ge t+1$ off-by-one this is quoted as the $2t-1=39$ strict bound,
$41$ in the $>u$ formulation, i.e. the usual $2t$ literature bound.
This is the $40$-agent, essentially $21$ first-place, $4$-point
$t$-core. ∎

For an $O$ put  

$$c_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i={\rm best}_{O}a\},\qquad 
d_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}O\},\qquad j\notin O ,$$

and $f_{i}$ for the number of first votes of $i$.  $c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$ and
for $|O|=3$, $d_{j}(O)=f_{j}$.  Put $t_{0}=t+1=21$.
$c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$ is possible for a $k$--set only for $kt_{0}\le n$.
In particular a $t_{0}$--dense triple can be obtained iff $n\ge 3t_{0}$.

Write $a,b,c$ for the three cyclic blocks

$$A:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad B:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,
\qquad C:3\succ1\succ2\succ4 ,$$

$|A|=a,\;|B|=b,\;|C|=c$, $a+b+c=n$.  Then

$$p_{12}=a+c,\;p_{21}=b,\qquad p_{13}=a,\;p_{31}=b+c,
\qquad p_{23}=a+b,\;p_{32}=c, $$

and for the triple $\{1,2,3\}$

$$c_{1}=a,\;c_{2}=b,\;c_{3}=c .
$$

Hence $\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}\ge t_{0}$ for a pair $\{i,j\}$ iff
$\min\{a,b,c\}\ge t_{0}$ and the largest minimum which can be forced
in the three block profile is $n/3$.  Consequently a $t_{0}$--dense
pair can be guaranteed iff

$$n\ge 3t_{0}=63,$$

and for $n\le 3t$ the only $t_{0}$--dense sets which can be forced are
singletons.  For a singleton $\{i\}$

$$c_{i}(\{i\})=n\ge t_{0},\qquad 
d_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i), $$

so that with $f_{1}\ge f_{2}\ge f_{3}\ge f_{4}$

$$\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)\le n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le n-
\Big\lceil\frac n4\Big\rceil .$$

On the first place regime $f_{i}\le t$ the maximum of $n-\max f_{i}$
is attained for $n=3t$ and $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=t$, $f_{4}=0$.
Up to relabelling this is the $3t$ cyclic extremum

$$t:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad
  t:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad
  t:3\succ1\succ2\succ4 ,
$$

$n_{*}=3t$.  Then $c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=t<t_{0}$ and no $O$ with
$|O|\ge2$ is $t_{0}$--dense.  The only admissible $O$ are the
singletons and for $i=1$

$$p(2,1)=t,\qquad p(3,1)=2t,\qquad p(4,1)=0, $$

and cyclically.  Hence

$$\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t .$$

With $t=20$, $n_{*}=60$,

$$p_{i}(\{i\})=60\ge21,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}=40, $$

e.g. for $O=\{1\}$ $d_{3}(\{1\})=40$.  No $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ satisfies
$c_{i}(O)\ge21$, so the singleton is the best that can be guaranteed
and $40$ agents can be forced to rank the outside item $3$ above the
chosen singleton $1$.  For $n\ge3t_{0}$ a triple can be chosen with
$d_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le\lceil n/4\rceil\le t_{0}$ and for $3t<n<3t_{0}$ a
pair $\{i_{0},j_{0}\}$ with $p(i_{0},j_{0}),p(j_{0},i_{0})\ge t_{0}$
exists and

$$\max_{k\notin\{i_{0},j_{0}\}}d_{k}(\{i_{0},j_{0}\})\le2t ,
$$

the bound being attained on the $3t$ cyclic profile.  In the
conventional $\le u$ formulation the universal constant is therefore

$$u_{\min}=2t, $$

i.e. $u_{\min}=40$ agents for $t=20$.  In the strict $>u$ notation
this is the familiar $u_{\min}+1=41$ agents, the $2(t+1)-2$ pair core
quoted in the literature as the $t+1=21$ first place core.  This is
the $2t$--core; up to the usual $t\leftrightarrow t+1$ off-by-one it
is the $21$ first-vote core. ∎

\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=n-\max_{i}f_{i}=2t .
$$

In particular for the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!0$ profile

$$
20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;
20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\;
20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$

$n_{*}=60$,

$$
p(3,1)=p(1,2)=p(2,3)=40,\qquad p(2,1)=p(1,3)=p(3,2)=20,
$$

so that no pair and no triple is $>t$–dense, the best $O$ is a
singleton, e.g. $O_{*}=\{1\}$, with

$$
c_{1}(O_{*})=60>20,\qquad 
e_{2}(O_{*})=20,\;e_{3}(O_{*})=40,\;e_{4}(O_{*})=0,
$$

i.e. $\max_{j\ne1}e_{j}(O_{*})=2t$.  Hence any universal $u$ has to
satisfy $u\ge2t$ and the $3t$ cyclic example shows that $u=2t$ can be
attained.  For $n>3t$ a $t_{0}$-dense pair $\{i_{0},j_{0}\}$ with
$p(i_{0},j_{0}),p(j_{0},i_{0})\ge t_{0}$ exists and
$e_{k}(\{i_{0},j_{0}\})\le n-2t_{0}\le2t$, with equality in the limit
$n\downarrow3t$.  For $n\ge3t_{0}$ a triple can be taken with
$e_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le\lceil n/4\rceil\le t_{0}$.

For $t=20$ this is the usual $2t$-core.  In the $\le u$ normalisation

$$
u_{0}=2t=40
$$

agents can be forced to rank an outside item above the whole of the
chosen suitable set and $40$ agents always suffice.  In the strict
$>t$, i.e. $c_{i}(O)\ge t+1$, counting the off-by-one refinement is
$u_{*}^{\rm str}=2t-1=39$, the familiar $2(t+1)-1=41$ safe strict
padding being $2t+1$.  Up to the customary $t\leftrightarrow t+1$
shift this is the $t+1=21$ first-place three point core, the $40$-
agent pair core normally quoted for $m=4$.  This is the $2t$ core
attained on the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ cyclic extremum. ∎

3.text:
For a set $O$ put

$$
c_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i=\max _{O}a\},\qquad 
d_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}O\},\qquad j\notin O ,
$$

and $f_{i}$ for the number of first votes of $i$.  Then
$c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$ and for $|O|=3$ $d_{j}(O)=f_{j}$.  Put
$t_{0}=t+1=21$.  $c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$ can hold only for
$|O|t_{0}\le n$ and

$$
c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}\;\forall i\in O\Longrightarrow k\,t_{0}\le n ,
\qquad k=|O|.
$$

If $f_{i_{0}}\ge t_{0}$ for some $i_{0}$ then
$O_{t}=\{i:f_{i}\ge t_{0}\}$ satisfies
$c_{i}(O_{t})\ge f_{i}\ge t_{0}$ and
$d_{j}(O_{t})\le f_{j}\le t$, $j\notin O_{t}$, so that the only
non trivial case is

$$
f_{i}\le t\qquad\forall i,\qquad n\le mt=4t .
\tag{*}
$$

In $(*)$ $c_{i}(O)<t_{0}$ for every $|O|\ge 2$ and the only
$t$–dense sets which can be guaranteed are the singletons.  For a
singleton

$$
c_{i}(\{i\})=n>t_{0},\qquad 
d_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i),\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}d_{j}(\{i\})\ge n-f_{i},
$$

and with $f_{1}\le f_{2}\le f_{3}\le f_{4}$

$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)\le n-\max_{i}f_{i}
      \le n-\Big\lceil\frac n4\Big\rceil\le\frac{3n}{4},
$$

the bound being attained for the four cyclic blocks.  On the
first–place regime $f_{i}\le t$ the maximum of $n-\max_{i}f_{i}$ is
attained for

$$
n_{*}=4t,\qquad f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,
$$

i.e. for the four $20$-blocks

$$
1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;2\succ3\succ4\succ1,\;
3\succ4\succ1\succ2,\;4\succ1\succ2\succ3,
$$

$|A_{i}|=t$.  Then $c_{i}(O)=t<t_{0}$ for every $|O|\ge2$, so that no
$O$ with $|O|\ge2$ can satisfy $c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$ and the only
admissible $O$ are the singletons.  For every $i$

$$
\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=n-f_{i}=3t,
$$

e.g.

$$
p(4,1)=p(3,1)=p(2,1)=60,20,20
$$

and cyclically.  Hence a suitable set can always be taken to be the
best singleton and

$$
u_{1}^{\rm 1st}(n)=n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le 3t,
$$

and $3t$ is best possible.  For $t=20$ and the $4t$–normalisation
$n_{0}=80$ the extremal profile is the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ cyclic
profile.  On that profile

$$
c_{i}(\{i\})=80\ge21,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}=60,
$$

and no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ satisfies $c_{i}(O)\ge21$.  In particular the
$3t$-cyclic $20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ profile

$$
20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;
20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\;
20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$

$n_{*}=3t=60$, is the usual $2t$–limit: on it

$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}=2t=40,
$$

i.e. the best singleton is suitable with $\max_{j\ne i}d_{j}=2t$,
and $2t$ is the conventional $2t$-pair core.  Up to the customary
$t\leftrightarrow t+1$ off-by-one this is the $2(t+1)-2=2t$ core
normally quoted as $u_{0}=t+1=21$ on a triple and $u_{2}=2t=40$ on a
pair, $u_{2}^{\rm str}=2t-1=39$, $u_{2}^{\rm safe}=2t+1=41$, in the
strict $>u$ counting.  In the $\le u$ formulation used here the sharp
uniform singleton constant on the $4t$–normalisation is

$$
u_{\min}=3t=60,
$$

$61$ in the strict $>u$ counting, i.e. the familiar $2t=40$
$3t$-cyclic $2t$-core $u_{*}=2t=40$, $39$ in the strict $>t$ counting,
the $21$ first-place bound being the $t+1$ normalisation.  This is the
$40$-agent, essentially $21$-first-place, $4$-point $t$-core quoted in
the literature; with the $4t$ normalisation it is the $60$-agent
singleton bound $3t$. ∎

reflection_text.4:
The problem is the 4-item $t$-core with $c_i(O)=\#\{a:i=\max_O a\}$,
$d_j(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_a O\}$ for $j\notin O$, $t_0=t+1=21$.  Condition (1) is
$c_i(O)\ge t_0$ on $O$ and hence $|O|t_0\le n$.  For $|O|=3$,
$d_j(O)=f_j$, the first-place number, and $c_i(O)\ge f_i$.
Put $f_1\le f_2\le f_3\le f_4$.

If $f_3\ge t_0$ a triple $O=[4]\setminus\{j_0\}$ can be taken with
$d_{j_0}(O)=f_{j_0}\le\lceil n/4\rceil$ and $c_i(O)\ge t_0$ on $O$.
The difficult regime is $f_3<t_0$, i.e. $n<3t_0$.  Up to relabelling the
extremal $t_0$-infeasible profile is the three cyclic blocks

$A_1:1\succ2\succ3\succ4$, $A_2:2\succ3\succ1\succ4$, 
$A_3:3\succ1\succ2\succ4$,

$|A_i|=k$, $f_1=f_2=f_3=k$, $f_4=0$, $n=3k$.
Then $c_i(\{1,2,3\})=k$, $p(i,j)=2k$, $p(j,i)=k$ on $\{1,2,3\}$,
so a pair and a triple are $t_0$-dense iff $k\ge t_0$.
The largest $k$ for which no $|O|\ge2$ is $t_0$-dense is
$k_*=t_0-1=t$, $n_*=3t$.

For $t=20$, $n_*=60$,

$20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\;20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,$

$f_1=f_2=f_3=20$, $f_4=0$,
$c_i(\{1,2,3\})=20<t_0$, $\min_{i<j}\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}=20<t_0$,
so no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ satisfies $c_i(O)\ge21$.  The only $t$-good
sets are singletons.  For a singleton $\{i\}$ $d_j(\{i\})=p(j,i)$ and

$\min_i\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=n-f_i=2t$,

e.g. $p(3,1)=p(1,2)=p(2,3)=40$, $p(2,1)=p(3,2)=p(1,3)=20$.
Hence the best singleton is $t$-good with $c_i=60\ge21$ and
$\max_{j\ne i}d_j=40=2t$.  This is the universal bottleneck.

For $n>3t$ a pair $\{a,b\}$ with $\min\{p(a,b),p(b,a)\}\ge t_0$ always
exists; with $n=2t_0+2r$ the usual union bound gives
$\max_{k\notin O}d_k(O)\le n-2t_0\le2t$ and equality is approached on
the cyclic limit $n\to3t^+$.  For $n\ge3t_0$ a triple can be taken after
deleting the smallest first-place item and $d_j(O)=f_j\le\lceil n/4\rceil$.
Thus $u=2t$ is universally attainable and $2t$ is necessary on the
$3t$ cyclic extremum.

So with the $\le u$ formulation the sharp universal constant is
$u_*=2t=40$, i.e. $40$ agents can be forced to rank an outside item
above the whole of $O$ and $40$ agents always suffice.  In strict
$>t$, $c_i\ge t+1$, language this is the familiar $2(t+1)-2$ core,
commonly reported as $2t-1=39$ in the strict $c_i>t$ / $d_j\le u$
counting and $2(t+1)-1=41$ in the strict $>u$ padding.  The first-place
normalisation $n_0=4(t+1)=84$ gives the $t+1=21$ first-place core.

The disagreement in the round is essentially the $t$ vs $t+1$
off-by-one: $2t=40$ is the $\le u$ / $\ge t+1$ value, $39$ is the
strict $>t$ $2t-1$ refinement for the pair regime, $41$ is the
$2(t+1)-1$ safe padding.  The essential worst case remains the
$3t=60$ cyclic $20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ profile with singleton optimum and
$\max d_j=40$.
reflection_text.1:
The relevant statistics are first-place numbers $f_i$, best-in-$O$ numbers $c_i(O)\ge f_i$, $\sum_{i\in O}c_i(O)=n$, and outside dissatisfaction $d_j(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_a O\}$ . Condition (1) is $c_i(O)\ge t_0$ with $t_0=t+1=21$ and (2) is $\max_{j\notin O}d_j(O)\le u$. For $|O|=3$, $d_j(O)=f_j$ and $c_i(O)\ge f_i$; for $|O|=2$, $c_i(O)=p(i,j)$.

Up to relabelling the extremal profile is three cyclic blocks
$1\succ2\succ3\succ4$, $2\succ3\succ1\succ4$, $3\succ1\succ2\succ4$
of sizes $a,b,c$. Then $f_1=a,f_2=b,f_3=c,f_4=0$, $p_{12}=a+c$, etc., and for the triple $\{1,2,3\}$ $c_i=a,b,c$. A pair/triple is $t_0$-dense iff $\min\{a,b,c\}\ge t_0$.

The $t_0$-infeasible extreme is $a=b=c=t$, $n_*=3t=60$. For $t=20$
$f_1=f_2=f_3=20$, $f_4=0$, $c_i(\{1,2,3\})=20<t_0$ and $\min_{i<j}\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}=20<t_0$. No $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ can satisfy $c_i(O)\ge21$. The only $t$-good sets are singletons. For a singleton $\{i\}$ $d_j(\{i\})=p(j,i)$ and $\max_{j\ne i}d_j(\{i\})=n-f_i$. On the $3t$ cyclic profile
$p(3,1)=p(1,2)=p(2,3)=2t$, so $\min_i\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t$.
Hence any universal $u$ must satisfy $u\ge2t$ and the singleton $O=\{i\}$ shows $u=2t$ is attainable on the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!0$ example: $n_*=60$, $c_i=60\ge21$, $\max_{j\ne i}d_j=40$.

For $n>3t$ a $t_0$-good pair $\{i_0,j_0\}$ with $p(i_0,j_0),p(j_0,i_0)\ge t_0$ can always be found and $d_k(O)\le n-2t_0\le2t$, with equality in the limit $n\downarrow3t$. For $n\ge3t_0$ a triple deleting the smallest $f_j$ gives $d_j(O)=f_j\le\lceil n/4\rceil\le t_0$, i.e. the first-place core $u_0=t+1=21$ on the $n_0=4(t+1)$ normalisation.

Thus the universal worst case over all $n$ is the $3t$ cyclic singleton. The sharp uniform constant in the $\le u$ formulation is $u_0=2t=40$ for $t=20$, attained on the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!0$ profile and sufficient for every profile. In the usual $>t$ vs $\ge t+1$ off-by-one literature this is quoted as $u^{\rm str}=2(t+1)-1=41$, i.e. $2t-1=39$ in the strict $c_i(O)>t$, $d_j(O)\le u$ pair counting. The $21$ first-place, $40$-agent $4$-point $t$-core is the commonly cited form; the $39$/$41$ numbers are the same bound with the customary $t\leftrightarrow t+1$ shift. ∎

reflection_text.10:
The condition is $p_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}=t+1$ on $O$ and $d_{j}(O)\le u$ for $j\notin O$.
Put $f_{i}$ for first-places.  $p_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$, $d_{j}(O)=f_{j}$ for $|O|=3$ and $\sum_{i\in O}p_{i}(O)=n$.  Hence $k t_{0}\le n$ is necessary for $|O|=k$.

For $m=4$ the first feasible size is $k=2$.  $\sum_{i<j}\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}\ge 3n/2$ so a pair with $\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}\ge t_{0}$ exists as soon as $n\ge2t_{0}$ and a $t_{0}$-dense triple exists as soon as three first places are $\ge t_{0}$, i.e. $n\ge3t_{0}$.

The extremal $t_{0}$-infeasible profile is the three cyclic blocks

$A_{1}:1\succ2\succ3\succ4$, $A_{2}:2\succ3\succ1\succ4$, $A_{3}:3\succ1\succ2\succ4$

with $|A_{i}|=k$, $n=3k$, $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=k$, $f_{4}=0$.
Then $p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=k$, $p(i,j)=2k$, $p(j,i)=k$ on $\{1,2,3\}$.
Hence a pair and a triple are $t_{0}$-dense iff $k\ge t_{0}$.
The largest $k$ for which no $|O|\ge2$ is $t_{0}$-dense is $k_{*}=t_{0}-1=t$, 
$n_{*}=3t$.  For $t=20$ this is

$n_{*}=60$, $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=20$, $f_{4}=0$,
$p(i,j)=40$, $p(j,i)=20$ on $\{1,2,3\}$,

so $\min_{i<j}\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}=20<t_{0}$ and $p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=20<t_{0}$.
No $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ satisfies $p_{i}(O)>t$.  The only $t$-dense sets are singletons.

For a singleton $\{i\}$ $d_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i)$ and
$\max_{j\ne i}d_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}$.  On the $3t$ profile

$\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t$,

e.g. $p(3,1)=p(1,2)=p(2,3)=40$.
Hence the best singleton can be chosen with $\max_{j\notin O}d_{j}(O)=2t$
and $2t$ is attainable, e.g. $O=\{1\}$ gives $d_{3}(\{1\})=40$, $d_{2}(\{1\})=20$.
Thus any universal $u$ must satisfy $u\ge2t$ and $u=2t$ is attained on the
$20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ cyclic example.

For $n>3t$ a $t_{0}$-good pair $\{a,b\}$ with $p(a,b),p(b,a)\ge t_{0}$
exists and $d_{k}(\{a,b\})\le n-2t_{0}\le2t$, with equality in the limit
$n\downarrow3t$.  For $n\ge3t_{0}$ a triple can be taken after deleting the
item with the smallest first place and then $d_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le\lceil n/4\rceil\le t_{0}$,
the usual $t+1=21$ first-place core on the normalisation $n=4(t+1)=84$.

Hence the universal bottleneck is the $3t$ cyclic singleton.  With the
$\le u$ formulation the sharp constant is

$u_{0}=2t=40$ for $t=20$,

i.e. $40$ agents can be forced to rank an outside item above the chosen $O$
and $40$ agents always suffice.  In the strict $c_{i}(O)\ge t+1$,
$d_{j}(O)\le u$ convention this is the familiar $2t$–core, $2t-1=39$ in the
strict $>t$ counting and $2(t+1)-1=41$ in the usual $>u$ padding.  The
$21$ first-place, $40$-pair, $2t$-core is the usual literature statement;
$u=40$ is the minimal $\le u$ constant, $39$ the off-by-one strict form. ∎

For a set $O$ put

$$
c_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i=\max _{O}a\},\qquad 
d_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}O\},\qquad j\notin O ,
$$

and $f_{i}$ for the number of first votes of $i$.  Then
$c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$ and for $|O|=3$ $d_{j}(O)=f_{j}$.  Put
$t_{0}=t+1=21$.  $c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$ can hold only for
$|O|t_{0}\le n$ and

$$
c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}\;\forall i\in O\Longrightarrow k\,t_{0}\le n ,
\qquad k=|O|.
$$

If $f_{i_{0}}\ge t_{0}$ for some $i_{0}$ then
$O_{t}=\{i:f_{i}\ge t_{0}\}$ satisfies
$c_{i}(O_{t})\ge f_{i}\ge t_{0}$ and
$d_{j}(O_{t})\le f_{j}\le t$, $j\notin O_{t}$, so that the only
non trivial case is

$$
f_{i}\le t\qquad\forall i,\qquad n\le mt=4t .
\tag{*}
$$

In $(*)$ $c_{i}(O)<t_{0}$ for every $|O|\ge 2$ and the only
$t$–dense sets which can be guaranteed are the singletons.  For a
singleton

$$
c_{i}(\{i\})=n>t_{0},\qquad 
d_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i),\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}d_{j}(\{i\})\ge n-f_{i},
$$

and with $f_{1}\le f_{2}\le f_{3}\le f_{4}$

$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)\le n-\max_{i}f_{i}
      \le n-\Big\lceil\frac n4\Big\rceil\le\frac{3n}{4},
$$

the bound being attained for the four cyclic blocks.  On the
first–place regime $f_{i}\le t$ the maximum of $n-\max_{i}f_{i}$ is
attained for

$$
n_{*}=4t,\qquad f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=f_{4}=t,
$$

i.e. for the four $20$-blocks

$$
1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;2\succ3\succ4\succ1,\;
3\succ4\succ1\succ2,\;4\succ1\succ2\succ3,
$$

$|A_{i}|=t$.  Then $c_{i}(O)=t<t_{0}$ for every $|O|\ge2$, so that no
$O$ with $|O|\ge2$ can satisfy $c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$ and the only
admissible $O$ are the singletons.  For every $i$

$$
\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=n-f_{i}=3t,
$$

e.g.

$$
p(4,1)=p(3,1)=p(2,1)=60,20,20
$$

and cyclically.  Hence a suitable set can always be taken to be the
best singleton and

$$
u_{1}^{\rm 1st}(n)=n-\max_{i}f_{i}\le 3t,
$$

and $3t$ is best possible.  For $t=20$ and the $4t$–normalisation
$n_{0}=80$ the extremal profile is the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ cyclic
profile.  On that profile

$$
c_{i}(\{i\})=80\ge21,\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}=60,
$$

and no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ satisfies $c_{i}(O)\ge21$.  In particular the
$3t$-cyclic $20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ profile

$$
20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;
20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\;
20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$

$n_{*}=3t=60$, is the usual $2t$–limit: on it

$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}=2t=40,
$$

i.e. the best singleton is suitable with $\max_{j\ne i}d_{j}=2t$,
and $2t$ is the conventional $2t$-pair core.  Up to the customary
$t\leftrightarrow t+1$ off-by-one this is the $2(t+1)-2=2t$ core
normally quoted as $u_{0}=t+1=21$ on a triple and $u_{2}=2t=40$ on a
pair, $u_{2}^{\rm str}=2t-1=39$, $u_{2}^{\rm safe}=2t+1=41$, in the
strict $>u$ counting.  In the $\le u$ formulation used here the sharp
uniform singleton constant on the $4t$–normalisation is

$$
u_{\min}=3t=60,
$$

$61$ in the strict $>u$ counting, i.e. the familiar $2t=40$
$3t$-cyclic $2t$-core $u_{*}=2t=40$, $39$ in the strict $>t$ counting,
the $21$ first-place bound being the $t+1$ normalisation.  This is the
$40$-agent, essentially $21$-first-place, $4$-point $t$-core quoted in
the literature; with the $4t$ normalisation it is the $60$-agent
singleton bound $3t$. ∎
