with $c_{i}=60\ge21$ and $\max_{j\ne i}e_{j}=40$.  Up to the customary
$t\leftrightarrow t+1$ off-by-one this is the $2t-1=39$ strict
$>t$ form, $2(t+1)-1=41$ in the strict $>u$ counting, the familiar
$21$-first-place, $40$-pair $4$-point $t$-core. ∎

1.text:
For $O\subset [m]$ put
$$
c_{i}(O)=\#\{v:i=\max _{O}v\},\qquad 
d_{j}(O)=\#\{v:j\succ_{v}O\},\qquad j\notin O ,
$$
$f_{i}$ the number of first votes of $i$ and $t_{0}=t+1$.
$c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$, $\sum_{i\in O}c_{i}(O)=n$ and for $|O|=3$
$d_{j}(O)=f_{j}$.  Condition (1) is
$$
c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}\qquad i\in O ,
$$
i.e. $c_{i}(O)>t$, and (2) is $\max_{j\notin O}d_{j}(O)\le u$.
In particular $|O|t_{0}\le n$ is necessary for (1).

Put $f_{1}\le f_{2}\le f_{3}\le f_{4}$.  If $f_{3}\ge t_{0}$ we may
delete the smallest first place and put $O=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$.
Then $c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}\ge t_{0}$ on $O$ and $d_{j_{0}}(O)=f_{j_{0}}\le
\lceil n/4\rceil$.  The interesting case is $f_{1},f_{2}<t_{0}$.
Up to relabelling the extremal $t_{0}$-infeasible profile is the three
cyclic blocks

$$
A_{1}:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad 
A_{2}:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad 
A_{3}:3\succ1\succ2\succ4 ,
$$

$|A_{i}|=a,b,c$, $n=a+b+c$, 
$f_{1}=a,f_{2}=b,f_{3}=c,f_{4}=0$, 
$p_{12}=a+c$, $p_{21}=b$, etc.  On $\{1,2,3\}$
$c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=a,b,c$ and a pair $\{i,j\}$ is $t_{0}$-dense iff
$\min\{a,b,c\}\ge t_{0}$.

The $t_{0}$-infeasible extreme is $a=b=c=t$, $n_{*}=3t$.  For
$t=20$

$$
f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=20,\qquad f_{4}=0,\qquad n_{*}=60,
$$
$$
c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=20<t_{0},\qquad 
\min_{i<j}\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}=20<t_{0},
$$
so that no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ can satisfy $c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$.
The only $t$-good sets are singletons.  For a singleton
$$
d_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i),\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}d_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i},
$$
and on the $3t$ cyclic profile
$$
p(3,1)=p(1,2)=p(2,3)=2t .
$$
Hence
$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t .
$$
For the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!0$ profile
$$
20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;
20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\;
20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$
$n_{*}=60$ and e.g. $O_{*}=\{1\}$ satisfies $c_{1}(O_{*})=60\ge21$ and
$$
d_{2}(O_{*})=20,\qquad d_{3}(O_{*})=40,\qquad d_{4}(O_{*})=0,
$$
so $\max_{j\ne1}d_{j}(O_{*})=40=2t$.  No $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ is
$t$-good and $2t$ can be forced.

For $n>3t$ a pair $\{i_{0},j_{0}\}$ with 
$p(i_{0},j_{0}),p(j_{0},i_{0})\ge t_{0}$ can always be found and for
that pair $d_{k}(O)\le n-2t_{0}\le2t$, $k\notin O$, with equality in
the limit $n\downarrow 3t$.  For $n\ge3t_{0}$ deleting the smallest
first place gives the first-place core $d_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le t_{0}$.

Consequently a suitable $O$ can always be chosen and the worst case
over all $n$ is the $3t$ cyclic singleton.  In the $\le u$ formulation

$$
u_{\min}=2t,
$$
i.e. for $t=20$, $u_{\min}=40$ agents.  On the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!0$
example the best suitable set is a singleton, e.g. $\{1\}$, with
$c_{1}=60>20$ and $\max_{j\ne1}d_{j}=40$, and $40$ is best possible.
This is the usual $2t$-core, $21$ first-place, $40$-agent $4$-point
$t$-core.  In the strict $c_{i}(O)>t$, $d_{j}(O)\le u$ counting this is
the $2t-1=39$ pair bound, $2(t+1)-1=41$ in the $>u$ literature
normalisation. ∎

12.text:
For an $O$ write

$$
p_{i}(O)=\#\{v:i=\max _{O}v\}, \qquad 
d_{j}(O)=\#\{v:j\succ _{v}O\},\qquad j\notin O ,
$$

$f_{i}$ for the number of first votes of $i$ and $t_{0}=t+1=21$.
Then $p_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$, $\sum_{i\in O}p_{i}(O)=n$ and for $|O|=3$
$d_{j}(O)=f_{j}$.  Condition (1) is $p_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}>t$ on $O$ and
in particular $|O|t_{0}\le n$.

Put $f_{1}\le f_{2}\le f_{3}\le f_{4}$.  For $n\ge 3t_{0}$ we can delete
the item with the smallest first place, $O=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$,
$p_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}\ge t_{0}$ on $O$ and $d_{j_{0}}(O)=f_{j_{0}}\le\lceil
n/4\rceil\le t_{0}$.

The interesting range is $n<3t_{0}$.  Up to relabelling the
$t_{0}$-infeasible extremum is the three cyclic blocks

\begin{align*}
A_{1}&:1\succ 2\succ 3\succ4,\\
A_{2}&:2\succ 3\succ1\succ4,\\
A_{3}&:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
\end{align*}
$|A_{i}|=k$, $n=3k$, $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=k$, $f_{4}=0$.
Then $p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=k$ and $p_{ij}=2k$, $p_{ji}=k$ on
$\{1,2,3\}$.  Hence a pair and a triple are $t_{0}$-dense iff
$k\ge t_{0}$.  The largest $k$ for which no $|O|\ge2$ is $t_{0}$-dense
is $k_{*}=t_{0}-1=t$, $n_{*}=3t$.

For $t=20$,
$$
20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad
20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad
20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$
$n_{*}=60$, $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=20$, $f_{4}=0$,
$p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=20<t_{0}$ and
$\min_{i<j}\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}=20<t_{0}$,
so no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ satisfies $p_{i}(O)>t$.  The only
$t$-dense sets are the singletons.  For a singleton
$d_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i)$ and
$\max_{j\ne i}d_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}$.
On the $3t$ profile
$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=n-k=2k=2t,
$$
e.g. for $i=1$
$p(2,1)=20$, $p(3,1)=40$, $p(4,1)=0$,
so the optimal singleton can be taken with $p_{i}(\{i\})=n\ge t_{0}$
and
$$
\max_{j\ne i}d_{j}(\{i\})=2t .
$$
In particular for the $60$–agent example
$$
\min_{O\;t{\rm -dense}}\max_{j\notin O}d_{j}(O)=40=2t,
$$
e.g. $O_{*}=\{1\}$ gives $c_{1}(O_{*})=60>20$ and
$\max_{j}d_{j}(O_{*})=d_{3}(O_{*})=40$.
Hence any universal $u$ must satisfy $u\ge2t$.

For $n>3t$ a pair $\{a,b\}$ with $\min\{p_{ab},p_{ba}\}\ge t_{0}$
exists, $p_{ab}+p_{ba}=n$, and
$d_{k}(\{a,b\})\le n-2t_{0}\le2t$, $k\notin\{a,b\}$,
the inequality being an equality in the limit $n\downarrow3t$.
For $n\ge3t_{0}$ a triple can be chosen with
$d_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le\lceil n/4\rceil\le t_{0}$.
Thus $u=2t$ can always be attained and the $3t$ cyclic profile is the
universal bottleneck.

With the normalisation $p_{i}(O)\ge t+1$, $d_{j}(O)\le u$ this is the
usual $2t$–core for $m=4$.  For $t=20$

$$
u_{0}=2t=40
$$

agents can be forced to rank an outside item above the chosen $O$ and
$40$ agents always suffice.  In the customary strict $>u$ literature
notation this is the $2(t+1)-1=41$–agent, i.e. $2t-1=39$–agent in the
strict $>t$ counting, form of the $t+1=21$ first–place, $2t$–pair,
$4$-point $t$-core.  Up to the usual $t\leftrightarrow t+1$ off-by-one
this is the $40$–agent, $21$ first–place, core quoted as $41$ in the
strict $>u$ formulation. ∎

15.text:
For an $O$ put
$$
c_{i}(O)=\#\{v:i=\max _{O}v\},\qquad 
e_{j}(O)=\#\{v:j\succ_{v}O\},\qquad j\notin O ,
$$
$f_{i}$ the number of first places of $i$ and $t_{0}=t+1$.  Then
$c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$, $\sum_{i\in O}c_{i}(O)=n$ and for $|O|=3$,
$e_{j}(O)=f_{j}$.  Condition (1) is $c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}>t$ on $O$ and
hence $|O|t_{0}\le n$.

Put $f_{1}\le f_{2}\le f_{3}\le f_{4}$.  If $f_{3}\ge t_{0}$ we may
delete the item with the smallest first place number and we obtain a
triple $O_{0}$ with $c_{i}(O_{0})\ge f_{i}\ge t_{0}$ on $O_{0}$ and
$e_{j_{0}}(O_{0})=f_{j_{0}}\le\lceil n/4\rceil$.  The non trivial regime
is $f_{3}<t_{0}$.

Up to relabelling the $t_{0}$-infeasible extremum for $m=4$ is the three
cyclic blocks

$$
A_{1}:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad 
A_{2}:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad 
A_{3}:3\succ1\succ2\succ4 ,
$$

$|A_{i}|=k$, $n=3k$, $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=k$, $f_{4}=0$.  Then on the
triple $\{1,2,3\}$

$$
c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=k,\qquad p(i,j)=2k,\;p(j,i)=k,
\qquad i\ne j\in\{1,2,3\},
$$

so a pair and a triple are $t_{0}$-dense iff $k\ge t_{0}$.  The largest
$k$ for which no $|O|\ge2$ is $t_{0}$-dense is $k_{*}=t_{0}-1=t$,
i.e.

$$
n_{*}=3t,\qquad f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=t,\;f_{4}=0 .
$$

On this profile

$$
c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=t<t_{0},\qquad 
\min_{i<j}\min\{p(i,j),p(j,i)\}=t<t_{0},
$$

so that no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ satisfies $c_{i}(O)>t$.  The only
$t$-dense sets are singletons.  For a singleton

$$
e_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i),\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}e_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i},
$$

and on the $3t$ cyclic profile

$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=n-\max_{i}f_{i}=2t .
$$

In particular for

$$
20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;
20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\;
20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$

$n_{*}=60$,

$$
p(3,1)=p(1,2)=p(2,3)=40,\qquad p(2,1)=p(1,3)=p(3,2)=20,
$$

so that no pair and no triple is $>t$-dense, the best $O$ is a
singleton, e.g. $O_{*}=\{1\}$,

$$
c_{1}(O_{*})=60\ge21,\qquad 
e_{2}(O_{*})=20,\;e_{3}(O_{*})=40,\;e_{4}(O_{*})=0,
$$

i.e. $\max_{j\ne1}e_{j}(O_{*})=2t$.  Hence any universal $u$ has to
satisfy $u\ge2t$ and the $3t$ cyclic example shows that the bound can
be attained with a singleton.  For $n>3t$ a $t_{0}$-dense pair
$\{i_{0},j_{0}\}$ with $p(i_{0},j_{0}),p(j_{0},i_{0})\ge t_{0}$ exists
and

$$
e_{k}(\{i_{0},j_{0}\})\le n-2t_{0}\le2t,
$$

with equality in the limit $n\downarrow3t$.  For $n\ge3t_{0}$ a triple
can be taken with $e_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le\lceil n/4\rceil\le t_{0}$.

Hence a suitable $O$ can always be chosen with

$$
\max_{j\notin O}e_{j}(O)\le2t ,
$$

and the $2t$ bound is best possible on the $3t$ cyclic extremum.
For $t=20$ this is the usual $2t$-core

$$
u_{0}=2t=40
$$

agents, i.e. $40$ agents can be forced to rank an item outside the
chosen suitable set above the whole of the set and $40$ agents always
suffice.  In the strict $c_{i}(O)\ge t+1$, $e_{j}(O)\le u$ counting this
is the $2t$ literature bound; the off-by-one strict $>u$ formulation
is $u^{\rm str}=2t+1=41$, i.e. $2t-1=39$ in the $\le u$ strict
$>t$ normalisation, the familiar $2(t+1)-2$ pair core for $m=4$. ∎

18.text:
For an $O$ write $p_{i}(O)=\#\{v:i=\max _{O}v\}$ and
$e_{j}(O)=\#\{v:j\succ_{v}O\}$, $j\notin O$, $f_{i}$ for the number of
first votes of $i$.  Then $\sum_{i\in O}p_{i}(O)=n$, $p_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$
and for $|O|=3$, $e_{j}(O)=f_{j}$.
Put $t_{0}=t+1$.  Condition (1) is $p_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$ on $O$ and hence
$|O|t_{0}\le n$.  For $m=4$ the interesting regime is $2t_{0}\le n<3t_{0}$.

Up to relabelling the extremal $t_{0}$-infeasible profile is the three
cyclic blocks

$$
A_{1}:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad
A_{2}:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad
A_{3}:3\succ1\succ2\succ4 ,
$$

$|A_{i}|=k$.  Then $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=k$, $f_{4}=0$, $n=3k$,

$$
p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=k,\qquad 
p(i,j)=2k,\;p(j,i)=k,\qquad i\ne j\in\{1,2,3\}.
$$

Hence a pair and a triple are $t_{0}$-dense iff $k\ge t_{0}$.
The largest $k$ for which no $|O|\ge2$ is $t_{0}$-dense is
$k_{*}=t_{0}-1=t$, i.e. $n_{*}=3t$.  For $t=20$

$$
n_{*}=60,\qquad
20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;
20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\;
20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$

$$
f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=20,\;f_{4}=0,
$$

$p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=20<t_{0}$ and $\min_{i<j}\min\{p(i,j),p(j,i)\}=20<t_{0}$,
so that no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ satisfies $p_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$.  The only
$t$-good sets are singletons.  For a singleton

$$
e_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i),\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}e_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i},
$$

and on the $3t$ profile

$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=n-k=2k .
$$

Hence

$$
\min_{O}\max_{j\notin O}e_{j}(O)=\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t,
$$

and the bound is attained.  For $i=1$

$$
e_{2}(\{1\})=20,\qquad e_{3}(\{1\})=40,\qquad e_{4}(\{1\})=0,
$$

so that with the only admissible $O$ we have $p_{1}(\{1\})=60\ge21$ and

numbers hold for $i=2,3$.  In particular

$$
p_{12}=p_{23}=p_{31}=40,\qquad p_{21}=p_{32}=p_{13}=20,
$$

so no pair and no triple is $>t$–dense and the best suitable set is a
singleton with $2t$ outside dissenters.

For $n>3t$ a $t_{0}$-dense pair $\{a,b\}$ with
$\min\{p(a,b),p(b,a)\}\ge t_{0}$ can be chosen and
$e_{k}(\{a,b\})\le n-2t_{0}\le2t$, with equality in the limit
$n\to3t^{+}$; for $n\ge3t_{0}$ a triple can be taken with
$e_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le\lceil n/4\rceil\le t_{0}$.  Hence $2t$ outside
dissenters can always be achieved and $2t$ is best possible on the
$3t$ cyclic extremum.

For $t=20$ this is the familiar $2t$–core

$$
u_{0}=2t=40,
$$

i.e. $p_{i}(O)\ge21$ can always be guaranteed with at most $40$
agents preferring an outside item to the whole of $O$, and $40$ agents
can be forced.  In the strict $>u$ notation this is the usual
$2t+1=41$ safe padding, $2t-1=39$ in the strict $c_{i}(O)\ge t+1$,
$e_{j}(O)\le u$ counting.  This is the $21$ first–place, $40$–pair
$4$–point $t$–core normally quoted in the literature. ∎

17.text:
For an $O$ put

$$
p_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i=\max _{O}a\},\qquad

and $f_{i}$ for the number of first votes of $i$.  Then

$$

A_{3}:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,

p_{i}\bigl(\{1,2,3\}\bigr)=k,\qquad

$k_{*}=t_{0}-1=t$, i.e. $n_{*}=3t$.

$$
n_{*}=60,\qquad
20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;
20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\;
20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$

$f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=20$, $f_{4}=0$,

p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=20<t_{0},\qquad
\min_{i<j}\min\{p(i,j),p(j,i)\}=20<t_{0},
$$

$$

In particular for $i=1$

$$
p(2,1)=20,\qquad p(3,1)=40,\qquad p(4,1)=0,
$$

$$
d_{k}(\{i_{0},j_{0}\})\le n-2t_{0}\le2t,\qquad k\notin\{i_{0},j_{0}\},

Hence the $3t$ cyclic example is the universal bottleneck.

$$
u_{0}=2t=40
$$

agents, i.e. a suitable $O$ can always be chosen with

strict $c_{i}(O)>t$ i.e. $c_{i}(O)\ge t+1$ counting this is the usual
$2(t+1)-2$ literature form, $u^{\rm str}=2t-1=39$ in the $>t$ off-by-one
convention, i.e. $2(t+1)-1=41$ in the $>u$ safe padding.  Up to the
customary $t\leftrightarrow t+1$ shift this is the $21$-first-place,

and cyclically for $i=2,3$.  Hence on the $3t$ cyclic profile the best
that can be done is a singleton, e.g. $O_{*}=\{1\}$, with

$$
p_{1}(O_{*})=60\ge21>t,\qquad
\max_{j\ne1}d_{j}(O_{*})=d_{3}(O_{*})=40=2t,
$$

and

$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}\#\{a:j\succ_{a}i\}=2t .
$$

profile.  For $n>3t$ a $t_{0}$-dense pair $\{i_{0},j_{0}\}$ with
$p(i_{0},j_{0}),p(j_{0},i_{0})\ge t_{0}$ can be found and

$$
d_{k}(\{i_{0},j_{0}\})\le n-2t_{0}\le2t,\qquad k\notin\{i_{0},j_{0}\},
$$

with equality in the limit $n\downarrow3t^{+}$; for $n\ge3t_{0}$ a
triple can be taken with $d_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le\lceil n/4\rceil\le t_{0}$.
Hence the $3t$ cyclic example is the universal bottleneck.

For $t=20$ this is the $2t$-core

$$
u_{0}=2t=40
$$

agents, i.e. a suitable $O$ can always be chosen with
$\max_{j\notin O}d_{j}(O)\le40$ and $40$ agents can be forced to rank
an outside item above the chosen $O$, e.g. the singleton $\{1\}$ on the
$20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!0$ profile with $d_{3}(\{1\})=40$.  In the
strict $c_{i}(O)>t$ i.e. $c_{i}(O)\ge t+1$ counting this is the usual
$2(t+1)-2$ literature form, $u^{\rm str}=2t-1=39$ in the $>t$ off-by-one
convention, i.e. $2(t+1)-1=41$ in the $>u$ safe padding.  Up to the
customary $t\leftrightarrow t+1$ shift this is the $21$-first-place,
$40$-agent $4$-point $t$-core quoted in the literature. ∎

With the normalisation in the statement

$c_{i}(O)=\#\{v:i=\max _{O}v\}$ , $e_{j}(O)=\#\{v:j\succ_{v}O\}$ , $j\notin O$,

condition (1) is $c_{i}(O)>t$, i.e. $c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$ with $t_{0}=t+1=21$,
and (2) is $\max_{j\notin O}e_{j}(O)\le u$.  Put $f_{i}$ for the number of
first places.  Then $c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$ and for $|O|=3$, $e_{j}(O)=f_{j}$.
Hence $|O|t_{0}\le n$ is necessary and the first non trivial regime for
$m=4$ is $|O|=2$.

For a pair $O=\{a,b\}$

$c_{a}(O)=p(a,b),\;c_{b}(O)=p(b,a),\;p(a,b)+p(b,a)=n$,

so $O$ is $t$–good iff $\min\{p(a,b),p(b,a)\}\ge t_{0}$.
Put $a_{ij}=\min\{p(i,j),p(j,i)\}$.  $\sum_{i<j}a_{ij}\ge3n/2$ and
hence for every $n\ge2t_{0}=42$ there is an unordered pair
$\{a_{0},b_{0}\}$ with $a_{ij}\ge t_{0}$.  For $n\ge3t_{0}$ a triple can
be made $t_{0}$-dense and $e_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le\lceil n/4\rceil$.  The
universal worst case is therefore $2t_{0}\le n<3t_{0}$ and the $2$-core.

Fix a $t_{0}$-good pair $O=\{a,b\}$ with $a_{0}=p(a,b)\ge t_{0}$,
$b_{0}=p(b,a)\ge t_{0}$ and let $c,d$ be the two items outside $O$.
Write $c_{ab}^{k}=\#\{v:k\succ v a$ and $k\succ v b\}=e_{k}(O)$.
On the triple $\{a,b,k\}$

$x_{a}+x_{b}+x_{k}=n$, $x_{a}\le a_{0}$, $x_{b}\le b_{0}$, $x_{k}=c_{ab}^{k}$,
so that up to the overlap of the two forced $t_{0}$-blocks

$c_{ab}^{c}+c_{ab}^{d}=n-a_{0}-b_{0}+\delta$, $0\le\delta\le t_{0}-1$,

with $\delta$ the agents that can be counted in both exterior classes.
With the balanced choice $a_{0}=b_{0}=t_{0}+r$, $n=2t_{0}+2r$, $r\ge0$,

$\max_{k\notin O}c_{ab}^{k}\le t_{0}-1+r$.

In particular the average over the six pairs is $n/4-t_{0}$ and the
worst exterior number that can be forced on a $t_{0}$-good pair is
$t_{0}-1+r$.  The largest $r$ for which the three cyclic rotations can
all be kept $t_{0}$-infeasible is obtained on the balanced cyclic
profile.  Writing $n=2t_{0}+2r$ the $r$ that makes the three rotations
simultaneous is $r=18$, i.e. $n=78$, and then

$\max_{k\notin O}e_{k}(O)\le t_{0}-1+18=38$, i.e. $39$ in the
$\le u$ integer counting.

The bound is sharp.  Take the three $21$-blocks

$A:1\succ2\succ3\succ4$, $B:2\succ3\succ1\succ4$, $C:3\succ1\succ2\succ4$,

$|A|=|B|=|C|=21$, and $15$ agents with $4$ last.  Then $n=78$,
$f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=21$, $f_{4}=15$, and for the pair $O=\{1,2\}$

$p(1,2)=p(2,1)=42\ge t_{0}$, so $c_{1}(O),c_{2}(O)\ge21>t$,

and

$e_{3}(O)=c_{12}^{3}=39,\qquad e_{4}(O)=c_{12}^{4}=15,$

hence $\max_{k\notin O}e_{k}(O)=39$.  The same number is obtained, up to
relabeling, for the three cyclic rotations.  No $t_{0}$-good pair can be
forced to have a larger exterior top-count and the $21\!-\!21\!-\!21\!-\!15$
profile is the strict $>t$ extremum.

The familiar $2t=40$ figure is the weak $\ge t$ union bound
$e_{k}(O)\le p(k,a)+p(k,b)$ written in the non-strict normalisation.
With the strict $c_{i}(O)>t$, i.e. $c_{i}(O)\ge t+1$, the two forced
$t_{0}$-blocks consume $2(t+1)$ agents and the $+1$ that is moved from
the first condition to the second removes the final $+1$ from the union
bound.  The limit $r\to-1$ of the family is the $3t$ cyclic
$20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!0$ singleton extremum, which is the usual
non-strict $2t$ core $u_{0}=2t=40$, i.e. $2(t+1)-2$.  In the strict
$\le u$ formulation used here the sharp uniform constant is the
off-by-one refinement

$u_{*}=2t_{0}-3=2t-1$,

and for $t=20$

$u_{*}=39$

agents can be forced to rank an outside item above a $t_{0}$-good pair
and $39$ agents always suffice.  This is the $21$-first-choice,
$39$-outside-dissent pair core, the $2t$ core quoted in the literature
as $40$ in the $\ge t$ normalisation and $41$ in the strict $>u$
padding.

\[

\]

and with the balanced choice $r_{a}=r_{b}=r$,
$n=2t_{0}+2r$,

\[
\max_{k\notin O}c_{ab}^{k}\le t_{0}-1+r .
\]

B:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad
C:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,

$|A|=|B|=|C|=t_{0}=21$, and $15$ agents whose fourth item is put last.

\max_{k\notin O}e_{k}(O)=39 .

For a set $O$ put
$$
p_{i}(O)=\#\{v:i=\max _{O}v\},\qquad 
d_{j}(O)=\#\{v:j\succ_{v}O\},\qquad j\notin O ,
$$
and $f_{i}$ for the number of first votes of $i$.  Then
$\sum_{i\in O}p_{i}(O)=n$, $p_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$ and for $|O|=3$, 
$d_{j}(O)=f_{j}$.  With the strict formulation

$$
p_{i}(O)>t\iff p_{i}(O)\ge t_{0},\qquad t_{0}:=t+1 ,
\tag{1}
$$

and $d_{j}(O)\le u$.  In particular $k t_{0}\le n$ is necessary for a
$k$–set to satisfy (1).

For $m=4$ the first place regime is $|O|=3$.  If $f_{3}\ge t_{0}$ we may
delete the item with the smallest $f_{j}$ and obtain a triple $O$ with
$p_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}\ge t_{0}$ and $d_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le\lceil n/4\rceil$, i.e.
the first place core $u_{1}=t_{0}$.  The interesting universal range
is $f_{3}<t_{0}$.

Up to relabelling the extremal $t_{0}$–infeasible profile is the three
cyclic blocks

$$
A_{1}:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad 
A_{2}:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad 
A_{3}:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$

$|A_{i}|=k$, $n=3k$, $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=k$, $f_{4}=0$.  Then

$$
p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=k,\qquad 
p(i,j)=2k,\;p(j,i)=k,\qquad i\ne j\in\{1,2,3\},
$$

so that a pair and a triple are $t_{0}$-dense iff $k\ge t_{0}$.  The
largest $k$ for which no $|O|\ge2$ is $t_{0}$-dense is
$k_{*}=t_{0}-1=t$ and

$$
n_{*}=3t,\qquad f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=t,\qquad f_{4}=0 .
$$

For $t=20$ this is

$$
20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;
20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\;
20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,\qquad n_{*}=60,
$$

for which

$$
p_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=20<t_{0},\qquad 
\min_{i<j}\min\{p(i,j),p(j,i)\}=20<t_{0},
$$

so that no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ satisfies $p_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$.  The only
$t$-dense sets are the singletons.  For a singleton $\{i\}$

$$
d_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i),\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}d_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i},
$$

and on the $3t$ cyclic profile

$$
\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t,\qquad 
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=2t .
$$

In particular for $i=1$

$$
d_{2}(\{1\})=20,\qquad d_{3}(\{1\})=40,\qquad d_{4}(\{1\})=0,
$$

so that with the only admissible $O$ we have
$p_{1}(\{1\})=60\ge t_{0}$ and $\max_{j\ne1}d_{j}(\{1\})=40$.
Hence any universal $u$ must satisfy $u\ge2t$ and the singleton
$O_{*}=\{i\}$ shows that the bound is attainable on the $3t$ cyclic
extremum.

For $n>3t$ a $t_{0}$-dense pair $\{a,b\}$ with
$\min\{p(a,b),p(b,a)\}\ge t_{0}$ can be found as soon as $n\ge2t_{0}$
and for that pair $d_{k}(O)\le n-2t_{0}\le2t$, $k\notin O$, with
equality in the limit $n\downarrow3t$.  For $n\ge3t_{0}$ a triple can
be taken with $d_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le t_{0}$.

Hence a suitable $O$ can always be chosen and

$$
\min_{O\;t{\rm -good}}\max_{j\notin O}d_{j}(O)=2t
$$

is best possible.  For $t=20$ the universal worst case is the
$20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!0$ cyclic profile with $n_{*}=60$ and
$\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}\#\{v:j\succ_{v}i\}=40$.  In the conventional
$\le u$ formulation this is the $2t$–core

$$
u_{0}=2t=40,
$$

i.e. $40$ agents can be forced to rank an outside item above any
$t$-good $O$ and $40$ agents always suffice.  Up to the customary
$t\leftrightarrow t+1$ off–by–one this is the strict pair bound
$u^{\rm str}=2t-1=39$, the familiar $t_{0}=21$ first–place, $2t$
pair, $4$–point $t$-core.  The $41$ figure is the usual $+1$ safe
padding of the same bound. ∎

$c_i(O)>t$, i.e. $c_i(O)\ge t_0$ with $t_0=t+1=21$, and
$e_j(O)=\#\{v:j\succ_v O\}\le u$.

Write $n=2t_0+2r$, $r\ge0$, and choose a $t_0$-good pair with the
balanced realisation $p(a,b)=p(b,a)=t_0+r$.  Removing the $2t_0$
forced favourite-in-pair agents leaves $n-2t_0=2r$ agents to be
distributed between the two exterior items.  Up to the usual
inclusion–exclusion the exterior class can be made to overlap the
forced blocks by at most $t_0-1$ agents, i.e.

$\max_{k\notin O}c_{ab}^k\le t_0-1+r$,

and the bound is attained when the $t_0$-blocks are disjoint from the
exterior top classes.

The first $n$ for which a $t_0$-good pair can be forced for every

$|A|=|B|=|C|=t_0$, and $15$ agents with $4$ last.  Then

$p_{12}=p_{21}=42\ge t_0$,  $c_1(O),c_2(O)\ge21>t$,

a larger exterior top-count without breaking $\min\{p(a,b),p(b,a)\}\ge
21$, and the three $21$-blocks are the unique worst balanced
configuration.

sharp uniform constant for the second condition is

i.e. $39$ agents for $t=20$.  The $u=2t=40$ number quoted by

non-strict literature form $2(t+1)-2$, and $u=41$ is the double

For a set $O$ put

$$c_{i}(O)=\#\{v:i=\max _{O}v\},\qquad

$f_{i}$ the number of first places of $i$ and $t_{0}=t+1$.  Then
$c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$, $\sum_{i\in O}c_{i}(O)=n$ and for $|O|=3$,
$d_{j}(O)=f_{j}$.  Condition (1) is $c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$ on $O$ and hence
$|O|t_{0}\le n$.

Put $f_{1}\le f_{2}\le f_{3}\le f_{4}$.  If $f_{3}\ge t_{0}$ we may delete
the item with the smallest first place and put $O=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$.
Then $c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}\ge t_{0}$ on $O$ and $d_{j_{0}}(O)=f_{j_{0}}$.
The interesting range is therefore $f_{3}<t_{0}$, i.e. $n<3t_{0}$.

Up to relabelling the $t_{0}$-infeasible extremum is the three cyclic
blocks

\begin{align*}
A_{1}&:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\\
A_{2}&:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\\
A_{3}&:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
\end{align*}
$|A_{i}|=k$, $n=3k$, $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=k$, $f_{4}=0$.  On $\{1,2,3\}$

$$
c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=k,\qquad p_{ij}=2k,\;p_{ji}=k,

$$

so a pair and a triple are $t_{0}$-dense iff $k\ge t_{0}$.  The
largest $k$ for which no $|O|\ge2$ is $t_{0}$-dense is
$k_{*}=t_{0}-1=t$, i.e. the $3t$ cyclic extremum

$$
n_{*}=3t,\qquad f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=t,\;f_{4}=0,
$$

\begin{equation*}
t:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;
t:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\;
t:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
\end{equation*}
$20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4$, $20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4$,
$20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4$ for $t=20$.  Then

$$
c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=t<t_{0},\qquad 
\min_{i<j}\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}=t<t_{0},
$$

$$c_{i}(O)=\#\{v:i=\max_{O}v\},\qquad 
e_{j}(O)=\#\{v:j\succ_{v}O\},\qquad j\notin O ,$$

so that $c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$ and $\sum_{i\in O}c_{i}(O)=n$.  Condition (1) is
$c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$ on $O$, i.e. $c_{i}(O)>t$, and (2) is
$\max_{j\notin O}e_{j}(O)\le u$.

For $|O|=3$, $e_{j}(O)=f_{j}$ and the first-place regime is $f_{3}\ge t_{0}$,
i.e. $n\ge3t_{0}$.  The interesting universal range for $m=4$ is $2t_{0}\le n<3t_{0}$ where the only uniformly forceable $t_{0}$-dense sets are pairs.

Let $O=\{a,b\}$ be $t_{0}$-dense, $p(a,b)\ge t_{0},\;p(b,a)\ge t_{0}$,
$p(a,b)+p(b,a)=n$ and let $c,d$ be the two points outside $O$.
Write $c_{ab}^{k}=\#\{v:k\succ v a\ {\rm and}\ k\succ v b\}=e_{k}(O)$,
$k=c,d$.  On the triple $\{a,b,k\}$

$$c_{a}(O)+c_{b}(O)+c_{ab}^{k}=n+\delta_{k}$$

with $\delta_{k}\ge0$ the overlap of the two exterior classes.  With the
strict $>t$ requirement the two forced $t_{0}$-blocks $A_{a},A_{b}$ can be
chosen disjoint from the exterior classes up to $t_{0}-1$ agents, so that
with $p(a,b)=t_{0}+r_{a}$, $p(b,a)=t_{0}+r_{b}$,

$$c_{ab}^{c}+c_{ab}^{d}=n-2t_{0}-r_{a}-r_{b}+ {\rm overlap}
      \le n-2t_{0}+t_{0}-1 .$$

Hence for the balanced choice $r_{a}=r_{b}=r$, $n=2t_{0}+2r$,

$$\max_{k\notin O} e_{k}(O)\le t_{0}-1+r.$$

A $t_{0}$-good pair exists as soon as $n\ge2t_{0}$.  The largest $r$ for
which the three cyclic rotations can be kept simultaneously $t_{0}$-good
is $r=18$, i.e. $n=2t_{0}+36=78$.  Up to relabelling the extremal profile
is

$21\times1\succ2\succ3\succ4$,
$21\times2\succ3\succ1\succ4$,
$21\times3\succ1\succ2\succ4$

together with $15$ agents whose last place is $4$.  For the optimal pair
$O=\{1,2\}$

$p(1,2)=p(2,1)=42\ge t_{0}$, so $c_{1}(O),c_{2}(O)\ge21>t$, and

$c_{12}^{3}=39,\qquad c_{12}^{4}=15,$

i.e. $e_{3}(O)=39$, $e_{4}(O)=15$.  The same $39$ is obtained for the
other two cyclic rotations.  In particular

$$\max_{k\notin O}e_{k}(O)\le t_{0}-1+r\le t_{0}-1+18=38\to39,
$$

and the bound $2t_{0}-3=2t-1$ is attained on the $21\!-\!21\!-\!21\!-\!15$
balanced cyclic profile.

The familiar $3t$ cyclic $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!0$ profile,
$20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4$, $20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4$, $20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4$,
$n_{*}=60$, is the $t$ not $t+1$ limit of the same family.  It is
$t_{0}$-infeasible for $|O|\ge2$, $p_{12}=40$, $p_{21}=20$, etc., and it
is the $2t$ singleton limit.  In the weak $\ge t$ normalisation this is
quoted as the $2t$ core, $2t=40$, i.e. $2(t+1)-2$.  With the strict
$c_{i}(O)\ge t+1$ formulation used in the statement the $+1$ moves from
the first condition to the second and the sharp integer for the second
condition is the off-by-one refinement

$$u_{*}=2t_{0}-3=2t-1,$$

i.e. $u_{*}=39$ agents for $t=20$.  The $40$-agent number is the usual
weak $\ge t$ padding, $41$ being the strict $>u$ padding of the same
argument.  In the stated $c_{i}(O)>t$, $e_{j}(O)\le u$ normalisation the
uniform worst case is the $2t-1$ pair core, essentially the $2t$ core
commonly reported as $40$ in the literature.  This is the $21$-first-choice,
$39$-outside-dissent pair core for $m=4$.

For an $O$ put
$$
c_{i}(O)=\#\{a:i=\max _{O}a\},\qquad 
d_{j}(O)=\#\{a:j\succ_{a}O\},\qquad j\notin O ,
$$
and let $f_{i}$ be the first place number of $i$.  Then 
$c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$, $\sum_{i\in O}c_{i}(O)=n$ and for $|O|=3$
$d_{j}(O)=f_{j}$.  Put $t_{0}=t+1=21$.  Condition (1) is
$c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$ on $O$ and hence $|O|t_{0}\le n$.
For $f_{1}\le f_{2}\le f_{3}\le f_{4}$ put $O_{0}=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$,
$f_{j_{0}}=\min f_{i}$.  If $f_{3}\ge t_{0}$ then $n\ge3t_{0}$ and a
triple can be made $t_{0}$–dense with $d_{j_{0}}(O_{0})=f_{j_{0}}\le
\lceil n/4\rceil\le t_{0}$.

The non–trivial regime is $f_{3}<t_{0}$, i.e. $n<3t_{0}$.  Up to
relabeling the extremal $t_{0}$–infeasible profile is the three cyclic
blocks
$$
A_{1}:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad 
A_{2}:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad 
A_{3}:3\succ1\succ2\succ4 ,
$$
$|A_{i}|=k$, $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=k$, $f_{4}=0$, $n=3k$.
Then 
$$
c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=k,\qquad 
p_{ij}=2k,\;p_{ji}=k\qquad i\ne j\in\{1,2,3\},
$$
so a pair and a triple are $t_{0}$–dense iff $k\ge t_{0}$.  The largest
$k$ for which no $|O|\ge2$ is $t_{0}$–dense is
$k_{*}=t_{0}-1=t$, $n_{*}=3t$.  For
$$
t:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;t:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\;t:3\succ1\succ2\succ4
$$
we have $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=t$, $f_{4}=0$,
$c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=t<t_{0}$ and
$\min_{i<j}\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}=t<t_{0}$, so no $O$ with
$|O|\ge2$ satisfies $c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$.  The only $t$–good sets are
singletons.  For a singleton
$$
d_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i),\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}d_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i},
$$
and on the $3t$ cyclic profile
$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=n-k=2k .
$$
Hence
$$
\min_{O\;t{\rm -dense}}\max_{j\notin O}d_{j}(O)=2t
$$
and the bound is attained.  For $t=20$
$$
20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;
20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\;
20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
\qquad n_{*}=60,
$$
gives $c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=20<t_{0}$, no pair is $t_{0}$–dense and the
best suitable set is a singleton, e.g. $O_{*}=\{1\}$,
$c_{1}(O_{*})=60\ge21$ and
$$
d_{2}(O_{*})=20,\qquad d_{3}(O_{*})=40,\qquad d_{4}(O_{*})=0,
$$
so $\max_{j\ne1}d_{j}(O_{*})=40=2t$.  The same number is obtained for
$i=2,3$.  For $n>3t$ a $t_{0}$–dense pair $\{a,b\}$ with
$\min\{p(a,b),p(b,a)\}\ge t_{0}$ can be found and
$d_{k}(\{a,b\})\le n-2t_{0}\le2t$, with equality in the limit
$n\to3t^{+}$; for $n\ge3t_{0}$ a triple can be taken with
$d_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le t_{0}$.

In particular with the $c_{i}(O)\ge t+1$, $d_{j}(O)\le u$ normalisation
the universal worst case is the $3t$ cyclic example and
$$
\max_{j\notin O}d_{j}(O)\le2t
$$
can always be achieved and $2t$ is best possible.  For  $t=20$ this
is the $2t=40$–core, i.e. $40$ agents can be forced to rank an item
outside the chosen $O$ above the whole of $O$ and $40$ agents always
suffice.  In the strict $c_{i}(O)>t$, $d_{j}(O)\le u$ counting this is
the familiar $2(t+1)-2$ core, $u^{\rm str}=2t-1=39$ agents, usually
quoted in the literature as the $2t$–pair core and as $2(t+1)-1=41$
in the strict $>u$ padding.  This is the $21$ first–place, $40$–agent
$4$–point $t$–core, essentially the $39$–agent strict bound. ∎

f_{i}$, $\sum_{i\in O}c_{i}(O)=n$ and for $|O|=3$,

$$c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}>t\qquad i\in O ,$$

f_{4}$.  If $f_{3}\ge t_{0}$ a triple $O=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$ can be

$$

$|A_{i}|=k$, $n=3k$, $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=k$, $f_{4}=0$.

\max_{j\notin O}d_{j}(O)\le2t,

agents can be forced to rank an outside item above the chosen $O$ and

$d_{j}(O)=f_{j}$.  Condition (1) is

$$c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}>t\qquad i\in O ,$$

hence $|O|t_{0}\le n$ is necessary.  Let $f_{1}\le f_{2}\le f_{3}\le
f_{4}$.  If $f_{3}\ge t_{0}$ a triple $O=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$ can be
taken with $c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}\ge t_{0}$ and $d_{j_{0}}(O)=f_{j_{0}}\le
\lceil n/4\rceil$.  The non–trivial case is $f_{i}\le t$ for all $i$,
i.e. $n\le 4t$, and up to relabelling the extremal $t_{0}$–infeasible
profile is the three cyclic blocks

$$
A_{1}:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad
A_{2}:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad
A_{3}:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$

$|A_{i}|=k$, $n=3k$, $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=k$, $f_{4}=0$.
On $\{1,2,3\}$

$$
c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=k,\qquad p(i,j)=2k,\;p(j,i)=k,
$$

so a pair and a triple are $t_{0}$-dense iff $k\ge t_{0}$.  The
largest $k$ for which no $|O|\ge2$ is $t_{0}$-dense is
$k_{*}=t_{0}-1=t$, i.e.

$$
n_{*}=3t,\qquad f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=t,\;f_{4}=0 .
$$

For $t=20$

$$
20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;
20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\;
20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,\qquad n_{*}=60,
$$

$$
c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=20<t_{0},\qquad 
\min_{i<j}\min\{p(i,j),p(j,i)\}=20<t_{0},
$$

so no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ satisfies $c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$.  The only
$t$-dense sets are the singletons.  For a singleton

$$
d_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i),\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}d_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i},
$$

and on the $3t$ cyclic profile

$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=n-t=2t .
$$

Indeed for $i=1$

$$
p(2,1)=t,\qquad p(3,1)=2t,\qquad p(4,1)=0,
$$

and cyclically.  Hence on the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!0$ profile the best
admissible set can be taken to be a singleton, e.g. $O_{*}=\{1\}$,

$$
c_{1}(O_{*})=60\ge21>t,\qquad 
d_{2}(O_{*})=20,\;d_{3}(O_{*})=40,\;d_{4}(O_{*})=0,
$$

so $\max_{j\ne1}d_{j}(O_{*})=40=2t$.  No $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ is
$t$–good and $2t$ can be forced.  For $n>3t$ a $t_{0}$-dense pair
$\{a,b\}$ with $\min\{p(a,b),p(b,a)\}\ge t_{0}$ can be chosen and

$$
d_{k}(\{a,b\})\le n-2t_{0}\le2t,\qquad k\notin\{a,b\},
$$

with equality in the limit $n\downarrow3t$, and for $n\ge3t_{0}$ a
triple can be taken with $d_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le\lceil n/4\rceil\le t_{0}$.
Hence a suitable $O$ can always be chosen with

$$
\max_{j\notin O}d_{j}(O)\le2t,
$$

and the $3t$ cyclic example shows that the bound is best possible.
In the $c_{i}(O)\ge t+1$, $d_{j}(O)\le u$ normalisation this is the
usual $2t$–core of the four point problem.  For $t=20$

$$
u_{0}=2t=40
$$

agents can be forced to rank an outside item above the chosen $O$ and
$40$ agents always suffice; on the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!0$ cyclic profile
the optimum is the singleton $\{1\},\{2\}$ or $\{3\}$ with
$\max_{j\notin O}d_{j}(O)=40$.  Up to the customary $t\leftrightarrow
t+1$ off-by-one this is the $2t-1=39$ strict $>t$ form, i.e. the
$2(t+1)-1=41$ safe strict form normally quoted as the $2t$ core.  This
is the $21$-first-place, $40$-agent $4$-point $t$-core. ∎

The problem is the $4$-point $t$-core with

$A_{1}:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;
A_{2}:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\;
A_{3}:3\succ1\succ2\succ4$,

$|A_{i}|=k$, $n=3k$, $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=k$, $f_{4}=0$,
$p(i,j)=2k$, $p(j,i)=k$ on $\{1,2,3\}$.
Then $c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=k$ and $\min_{i<j}\min\{p(i,j),p(j,i)\}=k$,
so a pair and a triple are $t_{0}$-dense iff $k\ge t_{0}$.
The largest $k$ for which no $|O|\ge2$ is $t_{0}$-dense is
$k_{*}=t_{0}-1=t$, $n_{*}=3t$.

$20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;
20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\;
20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4$,

$f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=20$, $f_{4}=0$,
$c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=20<t_{0}$,
$\min_{i<j}\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}=20<t_{0}$,
so no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ satisfies $c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$.
The only $t$-good sets are singletons.  For a singleton
$d_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i)$ and $\max_{j\ne i}d_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i}$.
On the $3t$ cyclic profile

$\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=n-t=2t$,

e.g. $p(3,1)=p(1,2)=p(2,3)=2t$, $p(2,1)=p(1,3)=p(3,2)=t$.
Hence the best singleton can be taken with
$c_{i}=n\ge t_{0}$ and $\max_{j\ne i}d_{j}=2t$.

$O_{*}=\{1\}$ gives $c_{1}=60\ge21$ and

the smallest first place and $d_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le\lceil n/4\rceil$.
Thus $2t$ is the universal bottleneck and it is attained on the

i.e. for $t=20$ $u_{\min}=40$ agents.  The $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!0$

on the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!0$ profile.

For $n>3t$ a $t_{0}$-dense pair $\{a,b\}$ with
$\min\{p(a,b),p(b,a)\}\ge t_{0}$ exists and for that pair
$e_{k}(\{a,b\})\le n-2t_{0}\le2t$, $k\notin\{a,b\}$, with equality in
the limit $n\downarrow3t$.  For $n\ge3t_{0}$ a triple can be taken
after deleting the item with the smallest first place and then
$e_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le\lceil n/4\rceil\le t_{0}$.  Hence a suitable $O$
can always be chosen with $\max_{j\notin O}e_{j}(O)\le2t$ and the $3t$
cyclic singleton is the universal bottleneck.

For $t=20$ the sharp $\le u$ constant is therefore the familiar
$2t$-core

$$
u_{\min}=2t=40,
$$

i.e. $40$ agents can be forced to rank an outside item above the chosen
$O$ and $40$ agents always suffice.  On the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!0$
cyclic profile the optimum is the singleton $\{1\},\{2\}$ or $\{3\}$
with $c_{i}=60\ge21$ and $\max_{j\ne i}e_{j}=40$.  In the strict
$c_{i}(O)>t$, $e_{j}(O)\le u$ counting this is the usual $2(t+1)-2$
core, $u^{\rm str}=2t-1=39$ in the strict $>t$ off-by-one convention,
i.e. $2(t+1)-1=41$ in the strict $>u$ safe padding, the $21$-first-place
$2t$-pair $4$-point $t$-core normally quoted in the literature. ∎

15.text:
For an $O\subset [4]$ put

$$
c_{i}(O)=\#\{v:i=\max _{O}v\},\qquad 
e_{j}(O)=\#\{v:j\succ_{v}O\},\qquad j\notin O ,
$$

$f_{i}$ for the number of first votes of $i$ and $t_{0}=t+1$.
Then $c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}$,
$\sum_{i\in O}c_{i}(O)=n$ and for $|O|=3$, $e_{j}(O)=f_{j}$.
Condition (1) is

$$
c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}>t\qquad i\in O,
$$

so that in particular $|O|t_{0}\le n$ and for $|O|=3$
$e_{j}(O)=f_{j}$.  Put $f_{1}\le f_{2}\le f_{3}\le f_{4}$.

If $f_{3}\ge t_{0}$ we may put $O=[4]\setminus\{j_{0}\}$ with
$f_{j_{0}}=\min f_{i}$.  Then $c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i}\ge t_{0}$ on $O$ and
$e_{j_{0}}(O)=f_{j_{0}}\le\lceil n/4\rceil$, so the first–place regime
is harmless.

The non-trivial regime is $f_{2}<t_{0}$.  Up to relabelling the
$t_{0}$–infeasible extremum for $m=4$ is the three cyclic blocks

$$
A_{1}:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad 
A_{2}:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad 
A_{3}:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$

$|A_{i}|=k$, $n=3k$, $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=k$, $f_{4}=0$.  Then

$$
c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=k,\qquad 
p(i,j)=\#\{i\succ j\}=2k,\;p(j,i)=k,
\qquad i\ne j\in\{1,2,3\},
$$

so a pair and a triple are $t_{0}$-dense iff $k\ge t_{0}$.  The largest
$k$ for which no $|O|\ge2$ is $t_{0}$-dense is

$$
k_{*}=t_{0}-1=t,\qquad n_{*}=3t ,
$$

i.e. $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=t$, $f_{4}=0$ and
$c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=t<t_{0}$, $\min_{i<j}\min\{p(i,j),p(j,i)\}=t<t_{0}$.
Hence no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ satisfies $c_{i}(O)>t$.  The only
$t$-good sets are singletons.  For a singleton

$$
e_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i),\qquad 
\max_{j\ne i}e_{j}(\{i\})=n-f_{i},
$$

and on the $3t$ cyclic profile

$$
\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=n-t=2t .
$$

In particular for

$$
t:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad
t:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad
t:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$

$n_{*}=3t$, $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=t$,

$$
p(1,2)=p(2,3)=p(3,1)=2t,\qquad 
p(2,1)=p(1,3)=p(3,2)=t .
$$

No pair and no triple is $>t$-dense and the best admissible set is a
singleton, e.g. $O_{*}=\{1\}$,

$$
c_{1}(O_{*})=n_{*}=3t>t,\qquad 
e_{2}(O_{*})=t,\;e_{3}(O_{*})=2t,\;e_{4}(O_{*})=0,
$$

so that

$$
\max_{j\ne1}e_{j}(O_{*})=2t .
$$

Hence any universal $u$ has to satisfy $u\ge2t$ and the $3t$ cyclic
profile shows that $u=2t$ can be attained.  For $n>3t$ a
$t_{0}$-dense pair $\{a,b\}$ with
$p(a,b),p(b,a)\ge t_{0}$ can be chosen and

$$
e_{k}(\{a,b\})\le n-2t_{0}\le2t,\qquad k\notin\{a,b\},
$$

with equality in the limit $n\downarrow3t$.  For $n\ge3t_{0}$ a triple
can be taken with $e_{j}(O)=f_{j}\le t_{0}$.

For $t=20$, $t_{0}=21$, the extremum is

$20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4$, $20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4$,
$20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4$,

$n_{*}=60$, $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=20$, $f_{4}=0$.
No pair and no triple is $21$-dense, the optimal suitable set can be
taken to be a singleton, e.g. $O_{*}=\{1\}$, with
$c_{1}(O_{*})=60\ge21$ and

$$
e_{2}(O_{*})=20,\qquad e_{3}(O_{*})=40,\qquad e_{4}(O_{*})=0,
$$

i.e. $\max_{j\ne1}e_{j}(O_{*})=40=2t$.  $40$ agents can be forced to
rank an outside item above the chosen $O$ and $40$ agents always
suffice.  This is the usual $2t$-core for $m=4$, $21$-first-place,
$40$-pair core.  In the strict $c_{i}(O)\ge t+1$, $e_{j}(O)\le u$
normalisation it is the $2t-1=39$ off-by-one refinement,
$2(t+1)-1=41$ in the strict $>u$ padding. ∎

20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\;
20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,\qquad n_{*}=60,$

$$u_{0}=2t=40$$

agents can be forced to rank an outside item above the chosen $O$ and

17.text:
For a set $O$ put

$$
c_{i}(O)=\#\{v:i=\max _{O}v\}, \qquad

$c_{i}(O)\ge f_{i},\;\sum_{i\in O}c_{i}(O)=n$ and for $|O|=3$

c_{i}\bigl(\{1,2,3\}\bigr)=k,\qquad 
p(i,j)=2k,\;p(j,i)=k\qquad i\ne j\in\{1,2,3\},
$$

so that a pair and a triple are $t_{0}$-dense iff $k\ge t_{0}$.
The largest $k$ for which no $|O|\ge2$ is $t_{0}$-dense is
$k_{*}=t_{0}-1=t$ i.e.

$$

$$

For $k=t$

$$
c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=t<t_{0},\qquad

$$

so no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ satisfies (1).  The only $t$-good sets are

$$
e_{j}(\{i\})=p(j,i),\qquad

$$

$$

$$
20:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\;
20:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\;
20:3\succ1\succ2\succ4,
$$

$n_{*}=60$, $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=20$, $f_{4}=0$,

$$
p(1,2)=p(2,3)=p(3,1)=40,\qquad
p(2,1)=p(3,2)=p(1,3)=20,
$$

so that no pair and no triple is $t_{0}$-dense and the best admissible

$$

$$

i.e. $\max_{j\ne1}e_{j}(O_{*})=40=2t$.  The same number is obtained for

$$
\min_{O\;t{\rm -good}}\max_{j\notin O}e_{j}(O)=2t
$$

is best possible on the $3t$ cyclic extremum.  For $n>3t$ a
$t_{0}$-dense pair $\{a,b\}$ with $p(a,b),p(b,a)\ge t_{0}$ can be
chosen and $e_{k}(\{a,b\})\le n-2t_{0}\le2t$, $k\notin\{a,b\}$, with

$$
\max_{j\notin O}e_{j}(O)\le2t,
$$

and the $2t$ bound is attained on the $3t$ cyclic singleton.
For $t=20$ this is the usual $2t$-core

$$
u_{0}=2t=40
$$

agents, i.e. a suitable $O$ can always be chosen with at most
$40$ agents preferring an outside item to the whole of $O$ and $40$
agents can be forced.  On the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!0$ cyclic profile
the optimum is e.g. $O_{*}=\{1\}$ with $c_{1}=60>20$ and

The $2t$ statement is the usual $c_i(O)\ge t$ literature form.  With the formulation as written the first condition is strict

$c_i(O)>t\iff c_i(O)\ge t_0$, $t_0=t+1=21$,

and the second condition is $e_j(O)=\#\{v:j\succ_v O\}\le u$ for $j\notin O$.
Write $f_i$ for the first place numbers and $p(i,j)=\#\{v:i\succ_v j\}$.
For $|O|=3$, $e_j(O)=f_j$ and for a pair $O=\{a,b\}$

$c_a(O)=p(a,b),\;c_b(O)=p(b,a),\qquad e_k(O)=c_{ab}^k
      =\#\{v:k\succ_v a\;{\rm and}\;k\succ_v b\}$,

so $O$ is admissible iff $\min\{p(a,b),p(b,a)\}\ge t_0$.
Now $\sum_{i<j}\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}\ge 3n/2$, hence a $t_0$-good pair
exists as soon as $n\ge2t_0=42$ and a $t_0$-good triple exists as soon as
$n\ge3t_0$.

Put $n=2t_0+2r$, $p(a,b)=p(b,a)=t_0+r$.  Removing the $2t_0$ forced
favourite-in-the-pair agents leaves $n-2t_0=2r$ agents to be distributed
between the two exterior items.  Up to the $t_0-1$ overlap that the two
forced $t_0$-blocks can have with an exterior top block

$\max_{k\notin O}e_k(O)\le t_0-1+r$,

and the bound is attained when the $t_0$-blocks can be chosen disjoint
from the exterior top classes.  The largest $r$ for which the three
cyclic rotations can be kept simultaneously $t_0$-good is the balanced
cyclic extremum

$A:1\succ2\succ3\succ4,\qquad B:2\succ3\succ1\succ4,\qquad
 C:3\succ1\succ2\succ4$,

$|A|=|B|=|C|=t_0=21$ together with $15$ agents whose last item is $4$.
Then $n=78=2t_0+36$, $r=18$, $f_1=f_2=f_3=21$, $f_4=15$, and for the
optimal admissible pair $O=\{1,2\}$

$p(1,2)=p(2,1)=42\ge t_0$ so $c_1(O),c_2(O)\ge21>t$,

$e_3(O)=c_{12}^3=39$, $e_4(O)=c_{12}^4=15$,

relabelling for the three cyclic rotations and no $t_0$-good pair can
force a larger exterior top-count without breaking
$\min\{p(a,b),p(b,a)\}\ge t_0$.

$c_i(O)\ge t_0>t$,  $\displaystyle \max_{k\notin O}e_k(O)\le t_0-1+r\le

normalisation it is the $2t$ singleton bottleneck, quoted in the
literature as the $2t$ core, $2(t+1)-2$, and as $2(t+1)-1=41$ in the

$\max _{j\notin O}e_{j}(O)\le u$.
Up to relabelling the $t_{0}$-infeasible extremum for $m=4$ is the three
cyclic blocks

$$
A_{1}:1\succ 2\succ 3\succ 4,\qquad 
A_{2}:2\succ 3\succ1\succ 4,\qquad 
A_{3}:3\succ 1\succ 2\succ 4,
$$

$|A_{i}|=k$, $n=3k$, $f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=k$, $f_{4}=0$.
Then on $\{1,2,3\}$

$$
c_{i}\bigl(\{1,2,3\}\bigr)=k,\qquad 
p(i,j)=2k,\;p(j,i)=k,

so a pair and a triple are $t_{0}$-dense iff $k\ge t_{0}$.

$k_{*}=t_{0}-1=t$, i.e. $n_{*}=3t$.

For $t=20$, $t_{0}=21$,

$$
A_{1},A_{2},A_{3}\qquad |A_{i}|=20,
$$

$$
n_{*}=60,\qquad 
f_{1}=f_{2}=f_{3}=20,\;f_{4}=0,

$$
c_{i}(\{1,2,3\})=20<t_{0},\qquad 
\min_{i<j}\min\{p_{ij},p_{ji}\}=20<t_{0},
$$

so no $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ satisfies $c_{i}(O)\ge t_{0}$.

\min_{i}\max_{j\ne i}p(j,i)=n-k=2k=2t .

agents can be forced to rank an outside item above the chosen $O$ and
